nodes.label: NOTE: This file should not be edited
nodes.norm_label: note: this file should not be edited

nodes.label: Law 2 — Architecture is fixed; features extend, never redefine
nodes.rationale: A new pattern needs an ADR approved before code, so architecture cannot drift one feature at a time.
nodes.norm_label: law 2 — architecture is fixed; features extend, never redefine

nodes.label: Law 3 — Contracts before code
nodes.rationale: Fixed order requirements -> domain model -> API contract -> shared types -> migration -> implementation -> verification -> docs; the contract diff IS the API review surface.

nodes.label: Law 4 — Single source of truth
nodes.rationale: Duplicate definitions are defects, not conveniences: enums to contracts, visual values to generated tokens, schema to docs/04 + migrations, copy to the one i18n catalog.

nodes.label: Law 7 — Cross-platform lockstep (web + RN same change)
nodes.rationale: Both platforms ship from the same contract in the same change; exceptions require an owner ruling recorded where the decision was made.
nodes.norm_label: law 7 — cross-platform lockstep (web + rn same change)

nodes.label: Law 9 — Incremental schema & API growth
nodes.rationale: docs/04 is frozen DESIGN, not a build order; a table belonging to a module that has not started is a violation.

nodes.label: Decision hierarchy and tiebreakers
nodes.rationale: Per-package CLAUDE.md beats a cross-cutting rule because it is closer to the code; a dated ADR beats a doc.

nodes.label: Stop-and-ask triggers
nodes.rationale: Silently choosing between readings of an ambiguous spec is the failure the triggers exist to prevent; never invent a requirement.

nodes.label: Minimise blast radius
nodes.rationale: If something small needs edits across many unrelated files, the architecture is wrong.

nodes.label: tenant_id never travels in a request body
nodes.rationale: It comes from verified session claims, so a client can never assert another tenant.
nodes.norm_label: tenant_id never travels in a request body

nodes.label: One z.enum per business set
nodes.rationale: Consumers import the inferred type and never re-declare values, so a new value fails to compile rather than rendering blank.

nodes.label: Canonical error envelope + errorHttpStatusByCode
nodes.rationale: A route declaring a NON-base error code needs ContractException with that literal, or the wire silently carries the wrong code with a green typecheck.

nodes.label: Money crosses the wire as a 2-dp decimal string
nodes.rationale: Never a float — paisa-level reconciliation cannot survive binary rounding.
nodes.norm_label: money crosses the wire as a 2-dp decimal string

nodes.label: Protocol constants exported from contracts
nodes.rationale: OTP_LENGTH, PHONE_NSN_LENGTH and friends live in contracts so no client hard-codes them.

nodes.label: Zod pinned at 3.x, zod/v4 Biome-banned
nodes.rationale: ts-rest Zod-4 support is still RC (spike S3); lifting the pin collapses the typed client.

nodes.label: pgEnum values hand-mirror contract z.enums
nodes.rationale: db-no-upward forbids importing contracts into packages/db, so the two lists must move in the same slice.

nodes.label: Migrations are append-only and sha256-locked
nodes.rationale: Editing an applied file makes the runner refuse to run at all; a PreToolUse hook also blocks the edit.

nodes.label: Every tenant-owned table needs all four (tenant_id, composite index, RLS policy, grants)
nodes.rationale: There are no default privileges, so a forgotten grant fails closed rather than leaking.
nodes.norm_label: every tenant-owned table needs all four (tenant_id, composite index, rls policy, grants)

nodes.label: Tenancy defence in depth — guard, repository filter, RLS backstop
nodes.rationale: All three always: JWT claims, tenantId from context never client input, RLS via current_setting('app.tenant_id', true) fail-closed.
nodes.norm_label: tenancy defence in depth — guard, repository filter, rls backstop

nodes.label: Cross-tenant reads return 404, never 403
nodes.rationale: A 403 reveals that another tenant's row exists.

nodes.label: UUIDv7 ids generated app-side
nodes.rationale: Tables carry no DB-side id default, so raw SQL inserts must supply ids.

nodes.label: Append-only ledgers (audit_log, usage_events, sync_mutations)
nodes.rationale: They get no UPDATE or DELETE grants at all.

nodes.label: enum-parity invariant (live pg_enum vs contract schemas)
nodes.rationale: Checks both directions plus NO_CONTRACT_YET mapping; it is what stops one side moving alone now that db-no-upward blocks the import.
nodes.norm_label: enum-parity invariant (live pg_enum vs contract schemas)

nodes.label: GLOBAL_TABLES / table-tenancy-scan
nodes.rationale: A table is either tenant-scoped or listed global with its reason — there is no third option, and the scan fails on anything else.

nodes.label: One Lingui catalog (EN/HI/MR) for web and React Native
nodes.rationale: LOCALES derives from the contracts uiLanguageSchema — never restate the locale list (Law 4).
nodes.norm_label: one lingui catalog (en/hi/mr) for web and react native

nodes.label: Runtime <Trans id="English source"> on both platforms
nodes.rationale: @lingui/swc-plugin fails against this Next version; mixing macro and explicit-id usage for the same string forks duplicate .po entries and cost real translations on 2026-07-26.
nodes.norm_label: runtime <trans id="english source"> on both platforms

nodes.label: Never translate kW/kWh/kWp, brands, DISCOM names
nodes.norm_label: never translate kw/kwh/kwp, brands, discom names

nodes.label: Indian grouping (lakh/crore) via the shared formatter
nodes.rationale: Applies in every locale — never a locale-default thousands separator.
nodes.norm_label: indian grouping (lakh/crore) via the shared formatter

nodes.label: Language is per USER, not per tenant
nodes.norm_label: language is per user, not per tenant

nodes.label: Hindi/Marathi need 20–30% more width
nodes.rationale: A layout that only fits English is not done.

nodes.label: Run i18n extract before committing
nodes.rationale: CI fails if catalogs are not freshly extracted, and the diff is noisy when it catches you late.

nodes.label: No raw visual values — everything from @heliogrid/tokens
nodes.rationale: Tokens are GENERATED from design/ds-source and _ds_manifest.json is untrusted for values. Hex fails lint; arbitrary px and inline style are review-only because no honest gate exists (docs/10 §8).
nodes.norm_label: no raw visual values — everything from @heliogrid/tokens

nodes.label: Primary actions near-black; accent is never a button fill
nodes.rationale: Accent #5A4BFF is focus, links, selection, active tab and control fills only; iridescence is atmosphere, never information.
nodes.norm_label: primary actions near-black; accent is never a button fill

nodes.label: Light-only v1 and the 12px text floor
nodes.rationale: The 11px/700/uppercase/0.12em overline is the single exception (docs/10 §3).
nodes.norm_label: light-only v1 and the 12px text floor

nodes.label: Screens import only from the component indexes
nodes.rationale: A surface the mockups don't cover is COMPOSED from existing vocabulary, never new visuals; log the composition as a module ruling.
nodes.norm_label: screens import only from the component indexes

nodes.label: Container / presentational / logic in different files
nodes.rationale: A .tsx holding both a data-fetching effect chain and the markup it feeds is a review finding; web page.tsx is routing only (ADR-0022).
nodes.norm_label: container / presentational / logic in different files

nodes.label: Status/variant maps are Record<TheEnum, …>
nodes.rationale: A new contract value then fails to compile here rather than rendering blank.

nodes.label: UI 'done means' checklist
nodes.rationale: 375px and 1440px, loading/empty/error/offline designed, keyboard reachable, 44px targets, no hover-only meaning, Hindi without clipping, provenance on numbers, web and RN together.

nodes.label: Re-emit and commit the OpenAPI surface
nodes.rationale: The emit reads dist/, so build first or you emit the old surface from stale dist and see no diff for a change you did make. A stale committed surface is a lie told to every reader.
nodes.norm_label: re-emit and commit the openapi surface

nodes.label: pnpm check:openapi
nodes.rationale: Builds, emits, fails on a stale committed spec, and with oasdiff installed also flags breaking changes against origin/main — advisory, not a CI gate.

nodes.label: Keep the pgEnum in step with the contract enum
nodes.rationale: A value on one side only is a silent production defect — rows the API can never return, or API values the database rejects at insert.
nodes.norm_label: keep the pgenum in step with the contract enum

nodes.label: Sweep the typed clients with turbo typecheck
nodes.rationale: A call site that did NOT break where you expected it to is hand-rolling HTTP; a Record map that did not break is not exhaustive.
nodes.norm_label: sweep the typed clients with turbo typecheck

nodes.label: Judge breaking changes before shipping
nodes.rationale: Removing a field, tightening a type, renaming a key or changing a declared status code breaks every existing client; a genuine break needs an owner ruling stated in the change.

nodes.label: A new numbered file, never an edit
nodes.norm_label: a new numbered file, never an edit

nodes.label: Three verification runs (apply, idempotent re-apply, invariants)
nodes.rationale: The invariants run is the one that matters — it proves cross-tenant reads see zero rows, cross-tenant writes fail, missing tenant context fails closed, ledgers reject UPDATE. A skipped invariant that reports success is worse than no invariant at all.
nodes.norm_label: three verification runs (apply, idempotent re-apply, invariants)

nodes.label: /qa — plan in Claude, execute in agy, loop until clean
nodes.rationale: Green gates never prove behaviour; a slice that was never run was never verified. Ends on exactly one of two conditions: a clean full certify run, or three fix rounds with failures remaining.
nodes.norm_label: /qa — plan in claude, execute in agy, loop until clean

nodes.label: Phase 0 — preflight, fail loudly by name
nodes.rationale: A QA run that silently skips a surface is the exact failure the replaced files warned about; two programs are named agy and the IDE launcher exits zero while dispatching into a GUI panel no script can read.
nodes.norm_label: phase 0 — preflight, fail loudly by name

nodes.label: Antigravity CLI (agy) as the QA executor
nodes.rationale: Claude decides what to test and fixes what breaks; agy executes. --json-schema enforces the report shape at the CLI layer rather than trusting the prompt.
nodes.norm_label: antigravity cli (agy) as the qa executor

nodes.label: Phase 1 — blast radius computed from the working diff
nodes.rationale: Git is manual here so work is normally uncommitted on main; git diff main...HEAD resolves to nothing and an empty blast radius produces an empty plan that reads exactly like a clean run.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 — blast radius computed from the working diff

nodes.label: plan.json — the QA plan artifact
nodes.rationale: Severity is decided in the plan, never by the executor; anything touching money reconciliation, tenancy isolation or provenance tiers is authored blocker.

nodes.label: Zero-cell abort — steps counted per (surface × quadrant)
nodes.rationale: A plan may be small; it may not be lopsided. A surface that cannot be exercised is recorded as blocked with its reason, never silently omitted.
nodes.norm_label: zero-cell abort — steps counted per (surface × quadrant)

nodes.label: --add-dir omission is a perfect silent false pass
nodes.rationale: Without it the run reports status SUCCESS with "DONE", burns tokens, takes ~26 seconds and does nothing; num_turns reported 1 both when real work happened and when none did.
nodes.norm_label: --add-dir omission is a perfect silent false pass

nodes.label: Phase 4 — verify the report before believing it
nodes.rationale: A fast model's failure mode is reporting a pass it did not earn: a pass whose artifact is missing is rewritten to inconclusive, and one contradicted spot-check escalates the whole run as untrusted.
nodes.norm_label: phase 4 — verify the report before believing it

nodes.label: Phase 5 — triage into bug / product-question / false-positive / environment
nodes.rationale: A product-question is recorded in docs/13 or docs/15 rather than invented, and does not block a clean run; an environment failure does not consume a fix round.
nodes.norm_label: phase 5 — triage into bug / product-question / false-positive / environment

nodes.label: Hard stop after three fix rounds; never edit plan.json to hide a failure
nodes.rationale: Stated explicitly because a fix loop under pressure will eventually rationalize deleting a step; each round also re-runs a fresh blast radius for the code the fix touched.
nodes.norm_label: hard stop after three fix rounds; never edit plan.json to hide a failure

nodes.label: Phase 7 — retention and committed evidence
nodes.rationale: plan.json, runbook.md, report.json and triage.md are committed history; artifacts are deleted only after a clean certify pass and kept whenever a run escalated.

nodes.label: Executor prohibitions (runbook)
nodes.rationale: The executor never modifies application source or plan.json, never decides a step is unnecessary, and records observed values verbatim.

nodes.label: No artifact means inconclusive, never pass
nodes.rationale: skipped and inconclusive are always acceptable; a false pass never is.
nodes.norm_label: no artifact means inconclusive, never pass

nodes.label: report.json (executor output)
nodes.rationale: passes is step IDs only, failures carry the detail, and the report carries no severity field because severity is not the executor's to judge.

nodes.label: QA execution environment (web, api, qa_readonly psql, idb, adb)
nodes.norm_label: qa execution environment (web, api, qa_readonly psql, idb, adb)

nodes.label: The four quadrants a QA plan must contain
nodes.rationale: Merges two predecessors: /verify-app walked states and never attacked, qa-breaker attacked and never confirmed the feature worked.
nodes.norm_label: the four quadrants a qa plan must contain

nodes.label: Quadrant 3 — negative paths
nodes.rationale: Guards must be deny-by-default; error envelope and status must match the contract; cross-tenant access returns 404 because a 403 leaks that the row exists.

nodes.label: Quadrant 4 — adversarial
nodes.rationale: Authored assuming the implementation is wrong until proven otherwise: double-submit, offline, stale data, cross-tenant probes, absurd inputs, timers and lifecycle.

nodes.label: Pixel precision — measure, do not eyeball
nodes.rationale: Never ask a model whether a gap is 12 or 16px; Playwright getComputedStyle asserted against packages/tokens/dist/tokens.json is deterministic. Vision is reserved for clipping, overlap, truncation and layout collapse.
nodes.norm_label: pixel precision — measure, do not eyeball

nodes.label: Pull request checklist and evidence template
nodes.rationale: Traces to a D-decision and a mockup filename; the Evidence section demands step IDs and observed values and requires saying plainly what could NOT be run.
nodes.norm_label: pull request checklist and evidence template

nodes.label: CI quality job (lint · typecheck · test · build · openapi)
nodes.rationale: Runs against a real postgres:16 service so the tenancy invariants cannot skip; BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is a throwaway because the schema forbids a dev fallback for a secret.
nodes.norm_label: ci quality job (lint · typecheck · test · build · openapi)

nodes.label: CI ios job (simulator build, macOS lane)
nodes.norm_label: ci ios job (simulator build, macos lane)

nodes.label: CI check: applied migrations not modified, deleted or renamed
nodes.norm_label: ci check: applied migrations not modified, deleted or renamed

nodes.label: CI OpenAPI freshness gate (pnpm check:openapi)
nodes.rationale: Same script as local so CI and local can never diverge on what 'fresh' means; oasdiff is absent so only the freshness half gates the merge.

nodes.label: CI i18n extract guard (unextracted messages never merge)
nodes.norm_label: ci i18n extract guard (unextracted messages never merge)

nodes.label: BUILD FIRST before lint/boundaries
nodes.rationale: dependency-cruiser resolves a workspace import through the target's main/types which point at dist/, so before anything is built the edge does not exist and every rule aimed at a dist-shipping package reports clean — proven 2026-07-31 with db-access-in-repositories-only.

nodes.label: CI RN JavaScript bundle step
nodes.rationale: assembleDebug does not bundle JS, so until this step a broken import path, renamed asset or package-exports change passed CI green; typecheck does not walk the real module graph, only the bundler does.

nodes.label: shell: bash for pipefail on the xcodebuild lane
nodes.rationale: Without pipefail the step's exit status is tail's (always 0), so a Swift compile error, a missing Pod or a bad Info.plist produced a GREEN job and Law 7's only mechanical iOS proof could never fail.
nodes.norm_label: shell: bash for pipefail on the xcodebuild lane

nodes.label: CI Better Auth migrations step (7 plugin-owned tables)
nodes.rationale: Without it the tenancy scan only WARNS the tables are absent, so the tables it exists to vet are never inspected in CI. Seven not eight: only organization and phoneNumber plugins are enabled, so jwks is not created.
nodes.norm_label: ci better auth migrations step (7 plugin-owned tables)

nodes.label: HelioGrid constitution (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: These rules deliberately bias toward caution over speed; for a trivial change use judgment, but never skip 'you ran it' for anything a user can see.

nodes.label: Compose, don't rebuild
nodes.rationale: packages/ holds the vocabulary and app code spends it; a missing primitive is ADDED to the package, never inlined locally. A restricted-element lint error IS this rule speaking.

nodes.label: One definition per fact
nodes.rationale: A fact both platforms need is defined in a package BEFORE either screen uses it — never authored twice and reconciled later.

nodes.label: Screens are the unguarded surface
nodes.rationale: The gates check packages — their API shape, purity and importers. Almost nothing checks what a screen authors inline, and that is where every recent defect landed.

nodes.label: Verified means you ran it
nodes.rationale: Green gates never prove UI work: browser for web, both simulators for RN, curl for api. A red probe proves nothing until you read WHY it went red — a syntax error, an earlier gate, or the pipeline's own exit code all look like a catch.

nodes.label: Read call sites, not declarations
nodes.rationale: Two platforms reach the same behaviour through differently-named state, so comparing what each side DECLARES produces confident, wrong findings.

nodes.label: Simplicity first
nodes.rationale: No speculative features, abstractions for single-use code, unrequested configurability, or error handling for states that cannot occur. Does not contradict compose-don't-rebuild: reuse a primitive, do not invent one for a single caller.

nodes.label: Surgical changes
nodes.rationale: Every changed line traces to the request; clean up only what YOUR change orphaned, and mention unrelated dead code rather than deleting it.

nodes.label: Goal-driven execution
nodes.rationale: Because the repo has no unit tests, the success criterion is never 'write a test' but running the thing; weak criteria force constant clarification, strong ones let you finish without asking.

nodes.label: pnpm verify — the gate set
nodes.rationale: lint · boundaries · typecheck · test · build. Needs a live postgres or the invariants skip loudly, so a green run has NOT proven tenancy. Enumerate files with git ls-files, never a bare glob — zsh aborts the whole command on one unmatched pattern, which reads as clean.

nodes.label: Never weaken a gate to make a change pass
nodes.rationale: A gate that blocks you means the change is wrong.
nodes.norm_label: never weaken a gate to make a change pass

nodes.label: Product law (owner rulings)
nodes.rationale: Sent proposals keep their prices (a price-book update creates a new version); read + export work regardless of billing state — never hold data hostage; the server assigns business identifiers; no feature flags, entitlements are the only gating.

nodes.label: Provenance tier on every user-visible number
nodes.rationale: measured / derived / estimated / assumed — a reader must always know how a figure was obtained.
nodes.norm_label: provenance tier on every user-visible number

nodes.label: Money never renders stale
nodes.rationale: Design changed + quote not recomputed means the figure must read provisional.

nodes.label: One money path — BOM ↔ proposal ↔ tranches ↔ payments reconcile to the paisa
nodes.norm_label: one money path — bom ↔ proposal ↔ tranches ↔ payments reconcile to the paisa

nodes.label: Structural adequacy is never computed — an engineer signs off
nodes.rationale: Who + when is recorded and the disclaimer travels with every structure-bearing output.
nodes.norm_label: structural adequacy is never computed — an engineer signs off

nodes.label: No unit tests — tests/invariants is the only executable check
nodes.rationale: Owner directive 2026-07-29: never a .test.* or .spec.* file anywhere.
nodes.norm_label: no unit tests — tests/invariants is the only executable check

nodes.label: Files ≲450 lines, split by responsibility
nodes.rationale: Never *-part2/*2/*-extra: a split needing a number is the wrong split.

nodes.label: Config comes from @heliogrid/env
nodes.rationale: The only package that reads a raw source; scripts/check-env-access.mjs is the authority and apps/web/lib/env.ts is a deliberate exception because Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* only in code it compiles.

nodes.label: Mechanism order: type → lint rule → instruction → script
nodes.rationale: A script encodes today's tree and rots; a new checker script needs an owner ruling saying why no type and no lint rule can hold it.
nodes.norm_label: mechanism order: type → lint rule → instruction → script

nodes.label: Git is manual
nodes.rationale: Finishing the work is not a commit trigger and neither is 'fix it'; prefer several small commits because the diff is what the owner reads.

nodes.label: One review per change
nodes.rationale: A bug that reaches main is fixed as a bug, not as a trigger to audit the audit; multi-round adversarial review only on owner request by name.

nodes.label: Write to the gates, don't lint after the fact
nodes.rationale: 2-space · LF · width 100 · semicolons · single quotes · trailing commas · organized imports · import type · no any/!/==/console.log/unused symbols · noUncheckedIndexedAccess.
nodes.norm_label: write to the gates, don't lint after the fact

nodes.label: AGENTS.md — HelioGrid constitution (agent-facing copy)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical to root CLAUDE.md; the same constitution surfaced under the tool-neutral filename.

nodes.label: HelioGrid platform overview
nodes.rationale: CRM → survey → 3D Design Studio → proposal → tokenised customer link → AI voice follow-up → project tracking → payments; India-first (GST, DISCOM, PM Surya Ghar, TRAI/DND, ₹ lakh/crore, EN/HI/MR) but architected for global expansion.

nodes.label: Verified cold-start order for local development
nodes.rationale: Steps 2 and 3 are not optional: workspace packages resolve through their dist/, so a migrate on an unbuilt tree dies on MODULE_NOT_FOUND with nothing pointing at the cause.
nodes.norm_label: verified cold-start order for local development

nodes.label: Stack summary
nodes.rationale: NestJS · Next.js · bare React Native · ts-rest + Zod · Drizzle + Postgres · PowerSync · Better Auth + MSG91 OTP · BullMQ + Upstash · Fly.io Mumbai + Tigris · three.js/WebGPU · Exotel + Sarvam · Razorpay · Lingui.

nodes.label: Domain engines ported from Solar-App-POC
nodes.rationale: Geometry, electrical, BOM, energy and structure engines are a validated proof-of-concept port per docs/05, not new work.

nodes.label: @heliogrid/api — NestJS modular monolith, the only tenant-facing HTTP surface
nodes.rationale: One Nest module per bounded context; controllers implement ts-rest contracts and hold ZERO business logic — service layer then tenant-scoped repository layer beneath.
nodes.norm_label: @heliogrid/api — nestjs modular monolith, the only tenant-facing http surface

nodes.label: Cross-module imports go through <m>.public.ts
nodes.rationale: Never another module's service class; common/ is framework plumbing and may never import a module, with business behaviour living in packages/domain.

nodes.label: db-access-in-repositories-only fence
nodes.rationale: db + drizzle are legal ONLY in *.repository.ts; services take repositories by DI and never see a tx or a table. Cross-tenant work is isolated in *.admin.repository.ts.

nodes.label: ContractException must carry the literal code and an explicit status
nodes.rationale: The envelope filter reverse-maps status→code, so a bare ConflictException emitted CONFLICT while the contract promised ALREADY_ONBOARDED; and defaulting status from errorHttpStatusByCode (base codes only) returned 500 with the right code in the body. Typecheck was green both times; only an end-to-end curl caught it (2026-07-27).
nodes.norm_label: contractexception must carry the literal code and an explicit status

nodes.label: SessionGuard as APP_GUARD — deny by default
nodes.rationale: A new controller is authenticated automatically; @Public() is the only opt-out and is LOAD-BEARING on health, since without it Fly's probes 401 and the machine fails its checks.
nodes.norm_label: sessionguard as app_guard — deny by default

nodes.label: SessionResolver port (contracts/src/ports/session.ts)
nodes.rationale: The guard depends on the port, never on the auth module, and is bound in app.module.ts — Nest resolves a provider's deps in the module that DECLARES it, so declaring it in common/ fails at boot.

nodes.label: ADMIN_DB token fenced to *.admin.repository.ts
nodes.rationale: Pools live in common/db/ provided globally, but ADMIN_DB sits alone in admin.token.ts so admin-pool-fenced can restrict it. @heliogrid/db/uuid is exempt because uuidv7 is pure randomBytes.

nodes.label: tsx/esbuild emits no decorator metadata — every param needs @Inject
nodes.rationale: Including Reflector and class providers; hit 2026-07-26.
nodes.norm_label: tsx/esbuild emits no decorator metadata — every param needs @inject

nodes.label: @heliogrid/web — Next.js App Router, pure frontend/BFF
nodes.rationale: Route handlers exist ONLY for cookie/session BFF glue; everything domain-shaped calls apps/api through the ts-rest client, and shared decisions are imported from @heliogrid/domain rather than authored here.

nodes.label: app/ ROUTES, features/ OWNS
nodes.rationale: A page.tsx body is ≤50 lines (Biome noExcessiveLinesPerFunction): read route params, call one controller hook, render one screen. A feature is named for the CAPABILITY it owns, matching the API module that serves it so one name spans both sides.

nodes.label: Features imported only through a barrel
nodes.rationale: features/<feature>/index.ts or a screen barrel one level down — nothing deeper, enforced by dependency-cruiser.
nodes.norm_label: features imported only through a barrel

nodes.label: A barrel must not mix a Server Component and a 'use client' screen
nodes.rationale: Next attaches the client screen's chunk to EVERY page reaching the barrel and tree-shaking cannot remove it — /design shipped the whole gallery at 147 kB against a 102 kB baseline (2026-07-31). Symptom: two routes reporting IDENTICAL First Load JS.
nodes.norm_label: a barrel must not mix a server component and a 'use client' screen

nodes.label: "sideEffects": ["**/*.css"] is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: Each screen imports its own CSS, which is a side effect, so without the declaration webpack keeps every module a barrel names — all three auth routes shipped an identical 183 kB (2026-07-31).

nodes.label: lib/api-client.ts is the ONLY path — never hand-roll fetch
nodes.rationale: An untyped api<T>() with a hand-declared response type made contract drift invisible to typecheck; api-client rejects on non-2xx so a resolved value is always the declared success body. Read error copy with envelopeMessage(err).
nodes.norm_label: lib/api-client.ts is the only path — never hand-roll fetch

nodes.label: Enum-driven pickers iterate schema.options
nodes.rationale: Onboarding's SEGMENTS was an as-const array — merely subset-assignable — so a new tenantSegmentSchema value compiled green while being unselectable in the UI.

nodes.label: lib/env.ts must write process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_* out LITERALLY
nodes.rationale: Next substitutes textually at build time, so process.env[key] or a spread reads undefined in the browser and silently falls back to the schema default — a production URL would be ignored with nothing failing.
nodes.norm_label: lib/env.ts must write process.env.next_public_* out literally

nodes.label: /design renders dist/tokens.json
nodes.rationale: A token that doesn't render there doesn't exist.

nodes.label: @heliogrid/mobile — bare React Native, NO Expo anywhere
nodes.rationale: Field-first app; never expo packages, EAS, AsyncStorage for tokens, direct packages/db imports, or domain logic AUTHORED here.
nodes.norm_label: @heliogrid/mobile — bare react native, no expo anywhere

nodes.label: All data access behind src/data/repositories.ts
nodes.rationale: Screens never see fetch/SQLite/sync. Repository types are INFERRED from contracts — a hand-written HealthStatus interface duplicating the liveness 200 schema drifted silently when the contract gained a field.

nodes.label: src/ui/api-parity.ts — RN↔web component parity as a typecheck
nodes.rationale: Parity is asserted against @heliogrid/ui-api, not compared in a gallery; drift fails THIS app's typecheck and names the component.
nodes.norm_label: src/ui/api-parity.ts — rn↔web component parity as a typecheck

nodes.label: RN keeps src/screens/<name>/ (ADR-0022)
nodes.rationale: RN has no router-driven app/ directory, so screen folders already are web's features/ equivalent; the asymmetry is deliberate and must not be 'aligned'. Never a components.tsx or hooks.ts grab-bag — a file named for its layer instead of its job is the same defect as *-part2.

nodes.label: 80-line screen component cap (Biome)
nodes.rationale: A screen that fetches, holds state, renders and styles in one file passes every other gate — LoginScreen hit 446 lines and GalleryScreen 406 (2026-07-31). Extract the hook first: logic is what makes the file unreadable, not markup.

nodes.label: Auth tokens via src/auth/keychain-storage.ts only
nodes.rationale: Every fetch uses credentials:'omit' because iOS CFNetwork merges stored cookies into a 401 without absorbSetCookies; the keychain jar is the only cookie path.

nodes.label: apps/mobile pins zod 3.25.76 explicitly
nodes.rationale: Without it pnpm resolved @ts-rest/core's zod peer to the transitive zod 4 in the store and the typed client collapsed to never — every api.* call became a type error (2026-07-27).

nodes.label: AppText Devanagari run-splitting and the typography role
nodes.rationale: Geist/Noto TTFs are bundled and Devanagari must be verified on BOTH simulators. a11y/useValidAriaRole is off for this app because AppText's role is a TYPOGRAPHY role (body/h2/overline), not ARIA, and real RN a11y goes through accessibilityRole.
nodes.norm_label: apptext devanagari run-splitting and the typography role

nodes.label: mobile-app-entry-thin — App.tsx never imports a screen
nodes.rationale: App.tsx renders RootNavigator only; navigation is by typed route name from src/navigation/routes.ts, never prop callbacks.
nodes.norm_label: mobile-app-entry-thin — app.tsx never imports a screen

nodes.label: src/env.ts — the app's one configuration decision point
nodes.rationale: Bare RN has no runtime process.env, so env.ts hands a source to @heliogrid/env/native which owns schema and validation. There is deliberately no src/config/ — a new folder category would need an ADR (Law 2).
nodes.norm_label: src/env.ts — the app's one configuration decision point

nodes.label: Panel Layout (design steps 5-6)
nodes.rationale: The core 3D design surface: the designer places and tunes the array, safety objects and wiring to reach a valid, buildable layout. Panel and inverter come from step 4; the result feeds the BOM.

nodes.label: Solar access heatmap
nodes.rationale: Per-month solar access rendered as a 0-100% gradient with sun-hours and kWh/m2, so panel placement is judged on measured access rather than eyeballing the roof.

nodes.label: Shadow / shading simulation
nodes.rationale: Array-and-shadows view at a chosen time of day. A proposal built from this design can label its generation numbers as derived rather than estimated.

nodes.label: Auto-fill roof vs manual panel placement
nodes.rationale: Two entry routes: place panels by hand, or fill the roof to the step 4 target or the roof maximum. Clearing everything is destructive but undoable, so the confirmation names exactly what disappears (panels, strings, cable runs).

nodes.label: Pipeline funnel and win/loss report
nodes.rationale: Owner-dashboard report answering 'where deals leak', scoped by rep and period.

nodes.label: Lost-late vs disqualified-early separation
nodes.rationale: A warm, quoted deal that fell through is the costly kind; a lead ruled out before a quote is a different lesson entirely. The two reason lists are deliberately kept apart rather than merged into one loss-reason chart.

nodes.label: Profile and preferences (settings 8.8)
nodes.rationale: Not owner-only: every user reaches their own account screen. Mobile-first because field users live there.

nodes.label: Per-person language (EN / HI / MR)
nodes.rationale: Language is per person, not per company: a Marathi surveyor and an English owner share one tenant and each pick their own. Changing it re-renders the whole app instantly with no reload, and only that user's view changes.

nodes.label: Indian number and rupee formatting invariant
nodes.rationale: Numbers, dates and rupee grouping stay Indian in every locale, so switching language never changes what a figure means.
nodes.norm_label: indian number and rupee formatting invariant

nodes.label: Phone and email as login identity
nodes.norm_label: phone and email as login identity

nodes.label: Mark won - a won deal becomes a project
nodes.rationale: Two fields and one confirmation. Customer, design, accepted proposal and payment schedule all carry over so nothing is re-typed.
nodes.norm_label: mark won - a won deal becomes a project

nodes.label: Projects board by stage
nodes.rationale: Shows what is moving, what is stuck and where money is owed. Days-in-stage is the metric because a project installed but stuck a month is not 'nearly finished'.

nodes.label: Project detail
nodes.rationale: Everything about one project in one place with the next action obvious. Advancing a stage updates the customer progress link and makes the next payment tranche due.

nodes.label: Project payments - collect against tranches
nodes.rationale: The same tranche split set in the proposal, on the same client-payable total. A tranche becomes due the moment its milestone passes; money owed never blocks the customer's progress link - chase the person, not the view.

nodes.label: Project document checklist
nodes.rationale: Some documents arrive automatically from earlier stages; the rest are uploaded. The handover pack unlocks only when every document is verified. Subsidy sanction stays visible because it is the customer's money.

nodes.label: Project blockers
nodes.rationale: Every delay names who is waiting and the date it started, so responsibility stays visible. An explained delay is tolerable; a hidden one becomes a complaint.

nodes.label: Handover and project close
nodes.rationale: On completion the project closes and the customer's progress link flips to 'your system is live'. A closed project can be reopened, and the referral ask is placed here because the roof is new.

nodes.label: Customer progress link
nodes.rationale: A public link the customer holds that updates as stages advance and blockers are set. It stays open even when payment is overdue - data is never held hostage.

nodes.label: Blocker ownership (DISCOM / customer / material / us)
nodes.rationale: Four possible waiting parties including 'us - our own delay, recorded honestly'. The chosen party writes the honest waiting line onto the customer's progress link.

nodes.label: Deal-to-project carry-over
nodes.rationale: Customer, approved design, accepted proposal and the payment schedule move into the project untouched. Final value is pre-filled from the accepted proposal and editable; the install date is a target, verified on the site visit.

nodes.label: Project setup (design step 1 of 10)
nodes.rationale: Opens the 10-step design flow: customer, jurisdiction and tariff, system basics, branding and the confirmed roof location.

nodes.label: Remote survey carry-over prefill
nodes.rationale: Address, tariff and site details arrive pre-filled from the surveyor's remote survey, each field marked 'from survey' and editable if something changed.

nodes.label: Jurisdiction and tariff (DISCOM slabs)
nodes.rationale: Tariff auto-fills from the DISCOM (MSEDCL) slabs and is overridable when the customer's actual bill differs.

nodes.label: Google Solar site intelligence and coverage fallback
nodes.rationale: Coverage is checked per roof and imagery date/quality shown. No coverage does not block the job - it degrades to manual design mode.
nodes.norm_label: google solar site intelligence and coverage fallback

nodes.label: Roof pin and the 25 m move rule
nodes.rationale: Moving the pin more than 25 m means it is a different building, so roofs, obstructions and panels are cleared and solar data re-fetched. The destruction is stated up front and is immediately undoable.
nodes.norm_label: roof pin and the 25 m move rule

nodes.label: Proposal PDF document pages
nodes.rationale: The customer-facing artifact: cover with proposal number and preparer, system summary, generation and savings, investment, payment schedule, inclusions, timeline, terms, bank details and an optional technical page.

nodes.label: Indicative-proposal disclaimer
nodes.rationale: When generation and savings are estimated from system size and location rather than a shading simulation, the document says so and names what will confirm them (site survey and shadow analysis).

nodes.label: Proposal form-step pattern
nodes.rationale: Reusable shell for the simple form steps: overline, title, optional-step affordance, labelled fields with unit, preview, hint and error slots.

nodes.label: Locked fields sourced from the account
nodes.rationale: Fields that come from the company account read as deliberately locked ('from your account', 'auto') rather than looking like broken inputs.
nodes.norm_label: locked fields sourced from the account

nodes.label: Optional / skipped step state
nodes.rationale: Skipping is a first-class state with its own note and an 'add it' path, so a skipped step never reads as failure. Saved-but-not-printed data (e.g. bank details) is stated plainly.

nodes.label: AI auto-fill with reset-to-AI-values
nodes.rationale: Metrics and financials pre-fill automatically; any human override is badged 'Edited' and the original AI values remain restorable.

nodes.label: Provenance labelling of numbers
nodes.rationale: Each figure labels its own honesty - a real simulation from a design versus an estimate without one - and approximate values carry an explicit approximation marker.

nodes.label: Timeline phase editor (reorderable, gated)
nodes.rationale: Phases drag to reorder and every phase needs a title and description before the proposal can be generated.

nodes.label: Terms and conditions three-page limit
nodes.rationale: Terms are optional, appended after the proposal and before annexures, capped at three pages with a live page/character counter because overflow would be silently cut from the PDF.

nodes.label: Version comparison (changed vs unchanged)
nodes.rationale: Shows only what moved, with old/new/delta per row; unchanged sections are named and collapsed so 'reviewed and unchanged' is distinguishable from 'not looked at'.

nodes.label: Reason attached to each version
nodes.rationale: A written reason rides on every version so a price change still makes sense weeks later.

nodes.label: Accepted versions are immutable
nodes.rationale: Editing an accepted proposal never changes what the customer agreed to - the app creates the next version from it instead.

nodes.label: Proposal defaults and templates (settings 8.4)
nodes.rationale: Seven sections, each pre-filling a step of the proposal builder, so every new proposal opens roughly 90% filled and reps only change what is different for the customer.

nodes.label: Save-as-template round-trip from in-context edits
nodes.rationale: A template saved while editing a real proposal drops straight back into the defaults list, so the settings screen and the in-context editors stay one store rather than two.

nodes.label: Live preview of a proposal built from defaults
nodes.norm_label: live preview of a proposal built from defaults

nodes.label: Named tranche sets (must total 100%)
nodes.rationale: Reusable splits the builder offers as chips; each set is validated to total exactly 100% at the defaults level, not only in the builder.

nodes.label: Default timeline phases
nodes.rationale: The phase sequence every new project timeline starts with; net metering is called out as the long pole in a roughly 6-9 week end-to-end estimate.

nodes.label: Financial assumptions defaults (savings and financing)
nodes.rationale: India-sensible defaults pre-fill steps 3 and 5; subsidy follows the PM Surya Ghar slab automatically from the system size rather than being typed.

nodes.label: Proposal builder entry
nodes.rationale: 'Who is this for?' appears only when the builder starts from the Proposals list; started from a lead the customer is already known and that step is skipped.

nodes.label: 11-step proposal builder shell
nodes.rationale: Steps can be done in any order. Next never blocks; only Generate validates and jumps to the first problem, so a rep is never trapped on a step they cannot finish yet.

nodes.label: Three starting points (with design / without design / duplicate)
nodes.rationale: With a design is recommended because size, generation, savings and components fill from it. Without a design is faster but the numbers stay estimates until a survey confirms them. Duplicating a past proposal is the fastest route for repeat residential jobs.
nodes.norm_label: three starting points (with design / without design / duplicate)

nodes.label: Customer search across leads and customers
nodes.rationale: A no-match result offers 'start as new customer' and auto-creates the lead from the client details entered in step 10, so a stranger never blocks the quote.
nodes.norm_label: customer search across leads and customers

nodes.label: Resumable draft (step N of 11) on the lead
nodes.norm_label: resumable draft (step n of 11) on the lead

nodes.label: Generate is the only validation gate
nodes.rationale: Validation is deferred to one place. Per-step state (done / needs fixing / here) is surfaced on the rail so the rep can see the outstanding problems without being stopped by them.
nodes.norm_label: generate is the only validation gate

nodes.label: Proposal type: CAPEX vs OPEX / PPA
nodes.rationale: CAPEX is outright purchase; OPEX/PPA is per-unit billing and is gated behind a PRO entitlement rather than a feature flag.
nodes.norm_label: proposal type: capex vs opex / ppa

nodes.label: Proposal data steps 4, 5, 6 and 9
nodes.rationale: Metrics and financials fill by AI and label their own honesty; the timeline reorders and gates on empty fields; terms is optional and warns past three pages.

nodes.label: Proposal preview - what the customer sees
nodes.rationale: The exact document the customer will receive, checked before it goes out, with per-section jump-to-edit back into the builder step that owns each page.
nodes.norm_label: proposal preview - what the customer sees

nodes.label: Pre-share required-item gate
