nodes.label: HelioGrid (multi-tenant SaaS for Indian solar EPCs)
nodes.rationale: Most Indian EPCs run on Excel and WhatsApp; PM Surya Ghar creates an enormous under-digitised funnel, so one record that travels from lead to payment replaces the spreadsheet-and-rekeying pipeline.
nodes.norm_label: heliogrid (multi-tenant saas for indian solar epcs)

nodes.label: 3D Design Studio (the flagship)
nodes.rationale: Nothing is compromised against the studio: it is the engineering moat, so every tool and computed output must survive the port at full parity including 375px mobile.

nodes.label: Honesty Is a Feature
nodes.rationale: Competitors sell certainty; HelioGrid sells trustworthy numbers — hence provenance tiers on every figure, money never rendering while stale, and structural adequacy never computed.

nodes.label: India-First, Global-Ready
nodes.rationale: GST, subsidy slabs, DISCOM states and TRAI calling rules are injected market configuration rather than hard-coded, so a new market is configuration and not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Explicit Non-Goals (v1)
nodes.rationale: Named so nobody 'helpfully' builds them: inventory/PO/O&M, WhatsApp sending, custom roles, LiDAR measurement, discount approvals, feature flags, PPA billing, website/inbound-WhatsApp channels.

nodes.label: The Three Audiences (owner, employees, EPC's customer)
nodes.norm_label: the three audiences (owner, employees, epc's customer)

nodes.label: Org-Level Capacity-Tiered Pricing
nodes.rationale: Per-seat pricing punishes whole-company adoption, which is exactly the behaviour the single-record pipeline needs; incumbents already price per-org or per-capacity, so HelioGrid adopts the same axis and undercuts every rung.

nodes.label: Trial-Only, No Free Tier
nodes.rationale: OpenSolar's free product is funded by distributor placement and a payments cut — a transaction-layer business deliberately not entered; without that engine a free tier is pure metered COGS.

nodes.label: Soft-Block Cap Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Caps are upgrade signals and abuse bounds, never feature ransoms — reading, editing existing records and exporting never pause.

nodes.label: Metered COGS (voice minutes, AI detections, OTP)
nodes.norm_label: metered cogs (voice minutes, ai detections, otp)

nodes.label: Unit Economics — gross margin ≥80% at typical utilisation
nodes.rationale: Worst-case floors are accepted because the dominant small-tier cost is amortised fixed infra that falls with tenant density, and overage sits ≥40% above worst-case unit COGS so no tier can go margin-negative.
nodes.norm_label: unit economics — gross margin ≥80% at typical utilisation

nodes.label: Go-To-Market (ride PM Surya Ghar, replace Excel+WhatsApp)
nodes.norm_label: go-to-market (ride pm surya ghar, replace excel+whatsapp)

nodes.label: Modular Monolith on Fly.io bom
nodes.rationale: One deployable API means one Postgres transaction scope, no distributed sagas, one deploy pipeline and single-digit-ms internal calls — the only honest shape for a next-month launch run by AI agents.

nodes.label: Dependency Direction Rule (dependency-cruiser enforced)
nodes.rationale: packages/db and drizzle-orm are importable only from *.repository.ts so every query path is tenant-scoped by construction; a module reaches another only through its <m>.public.ts so a service-signature change cannot ripple across contexts.

nodes.label: Request Path Anatomy (web, mobile, customer link)
nodes.norm_label: request path anatomy (web, mobile, customer link)

nodes.label: Webhook Invariant Pipeline (verify → dedupe → enqueue → fast 2xx)
nodes.norm_label: webhook invariant pipeline (verify → dedupe → enqueue → fast 2xx)

nodes.label: Realtime SSE Channels
nodes.rationale: SSE chosen over WebSockets: unidirectional fan-out, no sticky sessions, auto-reconnect for free; WebSockets enter only if collaborative design editing lands.

nodes.label: Storage Architecture (Tigris, single-region pin sin)
nodes.rationale: No India region exists so sin is the nearest pin; DPDP Rules 2025 use a negative-list model permitting cross-border storage by default, and the DB holding primary PII stays in bom.

nodes.label: Design-Studio Data Flow (the flagship path)
nodes.rationale: Visual meshes are never truth; everything derived is a pure function of the JSONB payload and is not persisted, so the studio's moat gets the strictest invariants.

nodes.label: Nested Design Fingerprints (siteFp ⊂ geometryFp ⊂ layoutFp ⊂ electricalFp ⊂ designFp)
nodes.rationale: This mechanism IS the 'money never renders while stale' rule: a quote whose designFp no longer matches reads as provisional, enforced at the API rather than in the UI.
nodes.norm_label: nested design fingerprints (sitefp ⊂ geometryfp ⊂ layoutfp ⊂ electricalfp ⊂ designfp)

nodes.label: Market Packs (rules + catalog + templates + locale)
nodes.rationale: India-first, global-ready means concretely that no market fact is ever a module-level constant — contexts are injected parameters and dependency-cruiser blocks any other import path.

nodes.label: Extraction Seams (module boundaries = future service boundaries)
nodes.rationale: Do not extract anything before a scaling or isolation reason exists; billing and agent are the first candidates because every module surface is already a ts-rest contract slice.
nodes.norm_label: extraction seams (module boundaries = future service boundaries)

nodes.label: NestJS backend (api, worker, voice)
nodes.rationale: Owner directive; modular-monolith layout maps 1:1 to product domains and mature guards/pipes/interceptors carry authz, validation and rate limiting. Hono was the research's original pick and was overridden.

nodes.label: ts-rest contract layer + Zod 3.25 pin
nodes.rationale: The one Nest-native contract-first option giving both end-to-end typed clients and emitted OpenAPI 3.1; Zod stays pinned at 3.25.x because ts-rest Zod-4 support is still an RC.

nodes.label: Drizzle ORM + append-only migrations
nodes.rationale: SQL-first: Postgres RLS via SET LOCAL is natural, emitted SQL is inspectable by agents, and drizzle-zod bridges tables into the Zod contract schemas.

nodes.label: Fly postgres-flex 3-node cluster (deprecation risk accepted)
nodes.rationale: Fly-native-only directive plus Fly MPG having no bom region; Fly has DEPRECATED unmanaged Postgres, so 3-node repmgr HA, two backup layers and restore drills are mandatory mitigations, with logical replication as a documented escape hatch.

nodes.label: BullMQ + Upstash Redis fixed plan
nodes.rationale: Fly explicitly recommends fixed plans for BullMQ because PAYG per-request billing is inflated by polling; eviction must stay OFF because Upstash eviction silently breaks queues.

nodes.label: PowerSync self-hosted (Open Edition)
nodes.rationale: The decisive property is that the write path is our own NestJS connector, while PowerSync supplies the genuinely hard parts — durable local SQLite, upload queue, checkpoint consistency and the attachment state machine.

nodes.label: Better Auth self-hosted (organization + phoneNumber + jwt)
nodes.rationale: Phone PII never leaves India because it is a TS library on our own DB rather than a US SaaS; Clerk was rejected on DPDP liability and cost.

nodes.label: Bare React Native (no Expo, iOS + Android)
nodes.rationale: Owner directive excludes Expo, which removes EAS Build and makes the macOS iOS CI lane mandatory; the studio opens as an authenticated WebView rather than being rebuilt as a native canvas.
nodes.norm_label: bare react native (no expo, ios + android)

nodes.label: three.js + WebGPURenderer with WebGL2 fallback
nodes.rationale: WebGPU is baseline across browsers in 2026 and the swap is near one line with automatic fallback; TSL compute shaders power the GPU shadow-map shading path.

nodes.label: Lingui v5 (one catalog, Next.js + bare RN)
nodes.rationale: The only compile-based option covering both surfaces from one catalog; Paraglide has no first-class RN support, which was the dealbreaker.
nodes.norm_label: lingui v5 (one catalog, next.js + bare rn)

nodes.label: Exotel telephony + Sarvam AI speech/LLM
nodes.rationale: Strongest India carrier compliance and in-country audio/PII; Sarvam has the lowest WER in 13/15 Indian languages. Spike S5 corrected the plan: BYO is inbound forwarding only, AgentStream provides no DTMF-send, and the 1600-series is closed to non-BFSI.

nodes.label: Razorpay Subscriptions + Invoices
nodes.rationale: One India-licensed PA covering mandates, trials and invoices, and the cheapest recurring rail; Stripe still is not a general domestic India acquirer in 2026.

nodes.label: Playwright headless Chromium PDF rendering
nodes.rationale: Chromium's HarfBuzz is the only path that shapes Devanagari correctly; react-pdf is disqualified on long-standing broken conjuncts and matras.

nodes.label: Biome + dependency-cruiser + sherif + Turborepo Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Style/correctness, semantic layers, versions and physical encapsulation are enforced together without dragging an ESLint runtime back in.

nodes.label: Exact Version Pin Policy
nodes.rationale: pnpm save-prefix='' means exact versions everywhere and the lockfile is the single authority; sherif fails CI on cross-package drift so there is one version of everything.

nodes.label: docs/04 is FROZEN DESIGN, not a build order (Law 9)
nodes.rationale: Every table is the reference that keeps future modules coherent, but tables are AUTHORED only when their owning module's slice begins; designing ahead guarantees refactors once real slices meet reality.
nodes.norm_label: docs/04 is frozen design, not a build order (law 9)

nodes.label: tenants table (multi-tenant root, RLS root key)
nodes.rationale: tenants.id IS the Better Auth organization.id, created in the same transaction at signup — no mapping table, no drift.
nodes.norm_label: tenants table (multi-tenant root, rls root key)

nodes.label: users table (domain profile, 1:1 with auth user)
nodes.norm_label: users table (domain profile, 1:1 with auth user)

nodes.label: user_roles table (six stackable presets)
nodes.rationale: Permission is OR across held roles and visibility is the widest scope held; no per-user permission override table exists, deliberately (D28).

nodes.label: customers table (phone is identity, dedupe root)
nodes.rationale: Carries consent, DND, do-not-call and preferred_language so the ComplianceGate reads one row per dial; merged rows are tombstones, never deleted.
nodes.norm_label: customers table (phone is identity, dedupe root)

nodes.label: lead_stage state machine
nodes.rationale: Raw stage UPDATEs are forbidden — transitions run only through service-layer functions so reason-mandatory rules, reopen restore points and won→project creation happen atomically.

nodes.label: activities table (polymorphic append-only timeline)
nodes.rationale: Polymorphic JSONB rather than one table per event type: the timeline is rendered as one stream and never joined per-kind; a Zod discriminated union keeps payloads typed.

nodes.label: surveys table (versioned-append)
nodes.rationale: A revisit inserts a new version row and nothing mutates — this is also the PowerSync conflict story, so offline captures never fight over one row.

nodes.label: designs table (JSONB payload + mirrored query columns)
nodes.rationale: The design graph stays JSONB because it is a deep single-editor document mutated hundreds of times per session; relational decomposition would buy nothing and cost the ported normalize/fingerprint machinery.
nodes.norm_label: designs table (jsonb payload + mirrored query columns)

nodes.label: engineer_signoffs table (append-only structural honesty)
nodes.rationale: Structural adequacy is never computed — this table records who signed and when, and a design edit after approval drops signoff_status back to draft.

nodes.label: design_blocks table (scale-program zones)
nodes.rationale: Blocks and tables are relational and outside the payload because at 100 MW they are the server-side query surface — shading jobs read blocks without hydrating a multi-MB payload.

nodes.label: design_tables table (mounting tables; panels derived, never persisted)
nodes.norm_label: design_tables table (mounting tables; panels derived, never persisted)

nodes.label: proposals table (one object, two entry paths)
nodes.rationale: Staleness is derived, never stored: the latest version's pinned design_fp is compared against the live designs.design_fp.
nodes.norm_label: proposals table (one object, two entry paths)

nodes.label: proposal_versions table (immutable, append-only)
nodes.rationale: The snapshot is JSONB because it is a commercial document frozen at send time — read whole, rendered whole, and must never drift when catalogs move.

nodes.label: proposal_components table (the mandatory gate)
nodes.rationale: Components are relational rather than inside the snapshot because the mandatory-gate validation and BOM reconciliation query them by category.

nodes.label: tranches table (one money path, schedule → collection)
nodes.norm_label: tranches table (one money path, schedule → collection)

nodes.label: customer_links table (tokenised, no login ever)
nodes.rationale: One URL advances in place through proposal → progress → handover; public reads go through SECURITY DEFINER functions scoped to the link's single deal, never a broad RLS policy, and links are never revoked over unpaid money.

nodes.label: projects table (light by design: status + documents + money)
nodes.norm_label: projects table (light by design: status + documents + money)

nodes.label: project_payments table (append-only receipts ledger)
nodes.rationale: Append-only with reversal rows, never edited — this is the received side of the money path and feeds the locked money-invariant test.

nodes.label: price_book_versions table (versioned non-catalog rates)
nodes.rationale: Rates are JSONB per version — an immutable snapshot read whole by the BOM engine; price updates create a new version, never mutate in place, and sent proposals pin the version.

nodes.label: agent_configs table (versioned-append)
nodes.rationale: Configs are never edited in place; publishing inserts version n+1 and queued calls keep the version they were queued with (D36).

nodes.label: calls table (every call ledgered, human and agent)
nodes.norm_label: calls table (every call ledgered, human and agent)

nodes.label: routing_policies table (versioned-append call routing as tenant data)
nodes.norm_label: routing_policies table (versioned-append call routing as tenant data)

nodes.label: entitlements table (current effective limits)
nodes.rationale: Relational rather than JSONB because it is queried on the hot path for the soft-block check; plan capacity ceilings stay in plans.bundles so the entitlement_key enum remains metered-quota-only.

nodes.label: usage_events table (append-only metered ledger)
nodes.rationale: Range-partitioned by month with a producer-supplied idempotency key so duplicate emits are no-ops; rollups are derived and safe to rebuild because the ledger is the truth.

nodes.label: market_rules_packs table (platform, versioned market config)
nodes.rationale: Injected into the domain resolveRules(ctx) so the module-level global dies; publishing a new pack self-stales fingerprints and a new market is a new pack with zero schema change.

nodes.label: webhook_events table (platform ingress dedupe)
nodes.rationale: Unique (provider, external_event_id) turns at-least-once delivery into exactly-once processing: verify HMAC → insert (conflict = duplicate, skip) → fast 2xx → BullMQ processes.

nodes.label: sync_mutations table (offline-write idempotency ledger)
nodes.rationale: The PowerSync upload-queue write path checks this ledger before applying, so at-least-once upload becomes exactly-once apply.

nodes.label: ops_drills table (restore-drill evidence log)
nodes.rationale: Append-only because it is the evidence trail that backups actually restore — an untested backup is a rumour.

nodes.label: JSONB vs Relational — the ruling census
nodes.rationale: JSONB where a document is read and written whole (design payload, survey capture, proposal snapshot, price book, rules pack); relational where rows are summed, gated or queried (components, tranches, payments, blocks, entitlements).
nodes.norm_label: jsonb vs relational — the ruling census

nodes.label: Port Philosophy (port-with-tests, no algorithm changes)
nodes.rationale: A module is ported when its POC tests pass unmodified; port → verify → improve later as a separate change, because improving during the port makes every diff ambiguous between defect and enhancement.

nodes.label: ProjectionContext (equirect default, UTM/ENU alongside)
nodes.rationale: Introduced at port time because every coordinate consumer is being touched anyway; the default implementation is the existing equirectangular projector so ported tests stay byte-identical, with proj4 UTM/ENU selected for ground-mount and large sites.

nodes.label: De-globalization of resolveRules()/resolveCatalog()
nodes.rationale: Module-level global singletons are a correctness bug in multi-tenant SaaS because geometry, pricing and sizing must vary by tenant and market; every former call site now takes context as its last parameter, and a lint grep gate keeps the strings extinct.

nodes.label: Three-as-Math Ruling (keep three.js as CPU maths)
nodes.rationale: Porting to a neutral maths kernel during the port would violate the no-algorithm-changes rule and reopen exactly the class of drift the one-frame gate exists to prevent.
nodes.norm_label: three-as-math ruling (keep three.js as cpu maths)

nodes.label: normalizeProject (normalize-on-read, Exhaustive<T> guard)
nodes.rationale: Its guarantees are load-bearing: per-item drop-with-reason, the Exhaustive<T> field-naming trick that caught the discount-erasure bug, byte-identical fingerprint preservation, and a NaN guard on weather.

nodes.label: Nine Port Batches A–I with three gates each
nodes.norm_label: nine port batches a–i with three gates each

nodes.label: Golden-File Pinning (byte-identical snapshots)
nodes.rationale: Any diff in the structure or BOM golden snapshots after the port is a port defect, not an improvement.

nodes.label: Deliberately Not Ported (store, persistence, proxies, R3F)
nodes.rationale: The freemium planLimitKw gate is deleted from the RulesContext schema entirely — plan gating is a billing concern, never a design-capacity cap, so no kW clamp exists anywhere in domain.
nodes.norm_label: deliberately not ported (store, persistence, proxies, r3f)

nodes.label: Domain Purity Contract (enforced, not promised)
nodes.rationale: dependency-cruiser blocks NestJS/React/fetch/storage/process.env/db/contracts imports in packages/domain; allowed deps are polygon-clipping, three (math only) and proj4.

nodes.label: Offline Principles (reads local, writes queued, server owns money)
nodes.rationale: One mental model on mobile and web so AI agents implement one write path, not three; offline output is always labelled provisional because the server owns truth and money.
nodes.norm_label: offline principles (reads local, writes queued, server owns money)

nodes.label: PowerSync Deployment on Fly bom
nodes.rationale: A dedicated publication over synced tables only keeps WAL fan-out and bucket churn bounded; buckets live in their own database so vacuum churn never bloats the app DB.

nodes.label: Sync Streams (token-parameterised, server-enforced scoping)
nodes.rationale: Stream parameters come from the verified JWT so the client cannot widen scope; even role-widening for managers is token-derived, never a client-supplied filter.

nodes.label: NestJS Backend Connector (the write path is our code)
nodes.rationale: Every response including rejects acks the mutation so the client can drop it and let sync-down restore server truth; 5xx is reserved for genuine faults, never business rejection.
nodes.norm_label: nestjs backend connector (the write path is our code)

nodes.label: Conflict Matrix (versioned-append, LWW, 409 on design)
nodes.rationale: LWW is resolved by server apply order, never device clocks; captured_at is preserved for display and audit only.

nodes.label: Attachment Pipeline (capture → presign → upload → ack-then-prune)
nodes.rationale: The full-resolution local copy is deleted only after the survey_photos row syncs back down — proof the server owns it; never base64 through the stream, never pruning before ack.

nodes.label: What Is NOT Offline (money math, design editing on mobile)
nodes.rationale: No device ever prints a customer-facing price computed locally; entitlement state is cached with a 72h grace so a paid tenant is never soft-blocked by a dead zone.
nodes.norm_label: what is not offline (money math, design editing on mobile)

nodes.label: Failure Modes & Recovery (quarantine, slot loss, token expiry)
nodes.rationale: Quarantine, never crash, never silently drop — nothing a field user captured is ever unrecoverable; a different user signing in wipes the local DB first because tenant isolation beats convenience.
nodes.norm_label: failure modes & recovery (quarantine, slot loss, token expiry)

nodes.label: Ports & Adapters (one interface, one adapter per environment)
nodes.rationale: Domain code never sees a port; orchestration calls the port and feeds results into pure domain functions, so swapping an adapter is a one-line provider change plus config.
nodes.norm_label: ports & adapters (one interface, one adapter per environment)

nodes.label: PortResult status envelope (never throw across a port)
nodes.rationale: ok / unavailable / unconfigured / error are distinct states so a missing key degrades gracefully instead of looking like an outage; HTTP relays return 200 with the envelope.
nodes.norm_label: portresult status envelope (never throw across a port)

nodes.label: withMetering adapter wrapper
nodes.rationale: Metering is a fire-and-forget enqueue so it never blocks or fails the request; billable metrics run the entitlement check BEFORE the call, non-billable ones are metered anyway for quotas and COGS dashboards.

nodes.label: SolarDataPort (PVGIS — energy source of record)
nodes.rationale: PVGIS is the ONLY energy source and no adapter may introduce a second irradiance path without an ADR; unavailability falls back to a labelled estimate rather than blocking the design.

nodes.label: BuildingInsightsPort (Google Solar — enhancement, never dependency)
nodes.rationale: India coverage is patchy, so no feature may depend on Google Solar existing; flux/irradiance layers are never requested.

nodes.label: RoofDetectPort (DSM primary, Gemini fallback)
nodes.rationale: Both paths exit through validateArtifact — no AI output enters a Project any other way; Gemini runs at temperature 0 with an enforced response schema, a versioned prompt and no-guessing instructions because an empty result beats an invented roof.

nodes.label: TelephonyCorePort — capability-negotiated port family (ADR-0019)
nodes.rationale: Telephony is a platform capability, never one vendor-shaped interface: adapters declare what they truly support via getCapabilities() and business logic branches on the declaration, never on the vendor name.

nodes.label: Capability Degradation Ladder (binding)
nodes.rationale: A feature needing a missing capability degrades on a defined path — never throws, never silently no-ops: warm transfer falls to cold transfer plus push, IVR traversal without dtmfSend flags the call ivr_blocked for human follow-up.

nodes.label: ComplianceGate — ours, non-swappable
nodes.rationale: TRAI penalties land on the tenant as Principal Entity, so the gate lives in our code rather than the vendor's; it fails closed — stale DND scrub pauses promotional dialing and there is no override flag.

nodes.label: MessagingPort (ManualCopyAdapter v1, BYO-WABA v2)
nodes.rationale: Rendering the message and letting the rep paste it carries zero regulatory surface and zero cost; in v2 each tenant owns their own WABA so deliverability reputation is isolated and assets survive a provider switch.

nodes.label: PaymentLinkPort (BYO-Razorpay per tenant)
nodes.rationale: Funds settle customer → EPC's own merchant account, so the platform never touches funds and needs no RBI Payment Aggregator licence; Razorpay Route stays a documented alternate adapter only.

nodes.label: DocumentRenderPort (Playwright now, Typst swap)
nodes.rationale: The customer link always renders the proposal as web — the PDF is an artifact, never the only path to the number.

nodes.label: PushPort (FCM HTTP v1 + APNs)
nodes.rationale: Push is best-effort by contract; the notifications table is the source of truth, so a dropped push never loses information.

nodes.label: OtpPort (MSG91 SMS → WhatsApp fallback)
nodes.rationale: No silent degradation on the front door: both channels failing means login fails loudly with an ops alert, because OTP delivery failure rate is an alerting metric.

nodes.label: MapsPort (server-fetched satellite tiles stored in Tigris)
nodes.rationale: Fetching once per site capture gives stable 1:1 pixel mapping for detection, reproducible provenance (the tile a design was traced on never changes under it) and one billing event instead of per-render fetches.
nodes.norm_label: mapsport (server-fetched satellite tiles stored in tigris)

nodes.label: Threat Model T1–T8
nodes.rationale: Ranked by impact × likelihood for a multi-tenant Indian EPC SaaS holding phone PII, deal values to ₹92L+ and BYO payment credentials; nation-state actors and DDoS beyond Fly/Upstash limits are explicit non-threats for v1.

nodes.label: Phone-OTP authentication flow (one server flow, web and RN)
nodes.norm_label: phone-otp authentication flow (one server flow, web and rn)

nodes.label: Session Models (cookie, keychain bearer, 10-min JWT)
nodes.rationale: Sessions are server-side rows so deactivating a user kills every device inside one JWT TTL; the JWT claim set is the entire authz payload and nothing more.

nodes.label: Six-Role Capability Matrix (16 capabilities)
nodes.rationale: OR across roles, visibility is widest, no per-user exceptions ever — exceptions are how permission systems become unauditable; deactivate never delete so history keeps attribution.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Tenancy Defence (guard → repo → RLS)
nodes.rationale: No layer trusts the one above it: a bug in the repository layer becomes an empty result rather than a leak.

nodes.label: Postgres RLS backstop (FORCE RLS, NOBYPASSRLS boot assertion)
nodes.rationale: RLS silently no-ops for superusers and BYPASSRLS roles, and a table owner otherwise bypasses its own policies — hence FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, a separate migrator role, and a startup assertion that refuses to boot.
nodes.norm_label: postgres rls backstop (force rls, nobypassrls boot assertion)

nodes.label: Customer-Link HMAC Token (stateless validity, stateful authority)
nodes.rationale: Verification recomputes the MAC and checks exp, then loads the link row for revocation status — so a revoked link dies instantly regardless of exp; Accept is never trusted from the token alone.
nodes.norm_label: customer-link hmac token (stateless validity, stateful authority)

nodes.label: OTP Anti-Abuse Controls
nodes.rationale: All limits live in Upstash on the fixed plan with eviction OFF — a rate-limit key must never be evicted into an allow.

nodes.label: Secrets Management (Fly secrets + per-tenant DEK envelope)
nodes.rationale: Per-tenant credentials are AES-256-GCM encrypted with a DEK wrapped by a master key that exists only as a Fly secret on the app that must decrypt; decrypt in memory at the call site, never logged, never returned by any API, every decrypt audited.
nodes.norm_label: secrets management (fly secrets + per-tenant dek envelope)

nodes.label: DPDP Compliance Posture
nodes.rationale: Fiduciary for tenant users' PII, processor for the EPC's customer data; erasure is anonymisation rather than row deletion because financial and tax records must be retained for statutory periods.

nodes.label: Audit Log Coverage Checklist (11 event classes)
nodes.norm_label: audit log coverage checklist (11 event classes)

nodes.label: Supply Chain Controls (frozen lockfile, postinstall disabled)
nodes.rationale: dependency-cruiser boundaries double as anti-exfiltration: packages/domain cannot import network or storage modules, so a compromised transitive dep in domain code has no I/O path.
nodes.norm_label: supply chain controls (frozen lockfile, postinstall disabled)

nodes.label: Structured Logging (pino + ALS context + mandatory redaction)
nodes.rationale: Redaction paths live in one shared config rather than per-app copies; `fly logs` is ephemeral and never the system of record, so logs ship to Loki and a Tigris archive sink.
nodes.norm_label: structured logging (pino + als context + mandatory redaction)

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry Tracing (W3C traceparent end-to-end)
nodes.rationale: traceparent is stored in BullMQ job data so the worker resumes the trace — one trace covers 'user clicked Generate PDF → job → Playwright → Tigris'; voice sessions sample at 100% because volume is low and value per trace is high.

nodes.label: Alert List (page-worthy DB, queue, webhook, voice, OTP alerts)
nodes.norm_label: alert list (page-worthy db, queue, webhook, voice, otp alerts)

nodes.label: Custom Prometheus Metrics (names are the contract)
nodes.norm_label: custom prometheus metrics (names are the contract)

nodes.label: THE Postgres Runbook
nodes.rationale: Fly deprecated unmanaged Postgres and the owner chose Fly-native anyway, so these mitigations are mandatory in-scope work rather than optional hardening — the custom image is ours to rebuild when Fly stops maintaining flex.

nodes.label: Two Independent Backup Layers → Tigris
nodes.rationale: The backup bucket is pinned to a different region from the database so a bom regional loss cannot take data and backups together; logical dumps survive anything that corrupts the physical timeline.

nodes.label: Restore Drill (pre-launch gate + monthly, canary-row RPO proof)
nodes.rationale: A worker writes a timestamped canary row every minute, so now() − max(canary.at) on the restored DB is the empirically proven RPO rather than a stated intention.
nodes.norm_label: restore drill (pre-launch gate + monthly, canary-row rpo proof)

nodes.label: Failover Procedure (fence first, never promote against a live primary)
nodes.rationale: Split-brain is the only unrecoverable state in the runbook; two nodes is a degraded state, not a stable one.
nodes.norm_label: failover procedure (fence first, never promote against a live primary)

nodes.label: Disk-Full and OOM Playbooks
nodes.rationale: Cause #1 is always WAL retention from stalled archiving or an inactive replication slot; dropping PowerSync's slot is a last resort because it forces a full resync of every field device.

nodes.label: Escape Hatch — logical replication to managed Postgres
nodes.rationale: Triggered by two consecutive failed restore drills, an unexplained HA event, sustained bom capacity failures or ops load above ~2 person-days/month; plain Postgres end to end means nothing locks in.
nodes.norm_label: escape hatch — logical replication to managed postgres

nodes.label: DR Targets (RPO ≤5 min, RTO ≤1 h) — stated then proven
nodes.norm_label: dr targets (rpo ≤5 min, rto ≤1 h) — stated then proven

nodes.label: Deploys (one Fly app per service, rolling, migrations as release_command)
nodes.rationale: Every migration must be expand/contract compatible with the previous release because old machines serve traffic during the roll; with no feature flags, a bad merge rolls back rather than getting flagged off.
nodes.norm_label: deploys (one fly app per service, rolling, migrations as release_command)

nodes.label: Cost Monitoring (fixed lines, sizing baseline, per-tenant COGS)
nodes.norm_label: cost monitoring (fixed lines, sizing baseline, per-tenant cogs)

nodes.label: design/ds-source is the pixel-perfect source of truth
nodes.rationale: Where any doc and the vendored CSS disagree, the CSS wins; _ds_manifest.json is inventory only and never a source of values because it snapshotted the 1ms reduced-motion durations as canonical.
nodes.norm_label: design/ds-source is the pixel-perfect source of truth

nodes.label: Token Pipeline — packages/tokens GENERATES from vendored CSS
nodes.rationale: Never hand-transcribe: the package's own manifest proves re-transcription drifts. Token names survive verbatim because the mockups reference them and renaming breaks pixel-perfect traceability.
nodes.norm_label: token pipeline — packages/tokens generates from vendored css

nodes.label: Marked Token Extensions (Devanagari face, semibold, brand-wash, viz namespaces, AA overrides)
nodes.rationale: Each extension is emitted under an explicit marker so ds-source diffs stay clean; extension 6 is the only one that CHANGES a ds-source value rather than adding one, because both colours failed AA for text in shipped components.
nodes.norm_label: marked token extensions (devanagari face, semibold, brand-wash, viz namespaces, aa overrides)

nodes.label: Contrast Build Gate (DECLARED_PAIRS + coverage from component usage)
nodes.rationale: Contrast is computed, never eyeballed, and coverage is derived from component usage so a pairing nobody declared fails the build rather than going unchecked. Floors come from the role's WCAG requirement, never the measured value, which would weaken the gate to pass.
nodes.norm_label: contrast build gate (declared_pairs + coverage from component usage)

nodes.label: Brand Law (neutrals are the product, near-black primary action)
nodes.rationale: Restraint is the premium signal: iridescence is atmosphere only, hierarchy comes from luminance and softness rather than lines, and overlays blur toward white rather than using a dark scrim.
nodes.norm_label: brand law (neutrals are the product, near-black primary action)

nodes.label: Light-Only v1 (owner ruling A)
nodes.rationale: The ds system is light-only by law and by fact (zero dark tokens, color-scheme:light); the semantic-alias indirection is kept so a dark value set is a later drop-in with no component rewrite. The 'studio canvas stays dark' doctrine is dead.

nodes.label: 21-Component API of packages/ui (prop enums are the contract)
nodes.rationale: The ds JSX library is spec to implement, not code to import; Radix supplies a11y plumbing underneath while the visual layer is pure token-driven styling, and typed prop enums make violations compile errors rather than lint warnings.
nodes.norm_label: 21-component api of packages/ui (prop enums are the contract)

nodes.label: Four Behavioural Contracts (NumberField, DataTable caption, ariaLabel, focus)
nodes.rationale: The BOM and quote are commercial documents, so no anonymous tables; NumberField commits on blur because keystroke commits break precise numeric entry on mobile keyboards.
nodes.norm_label: four behavioural contracts (numberfield, datatable caption, arialabel, focus)

nodes.label: Lingui One-Catalog Architecture (packages/i18n)
nodes.rationale: Locale resolves per-USER rather than per-tenant so a Marathi surveyor and an English owner coexist in one tenant; missing translations fall back to English at runtime, never a bare key and never a crash.

nodes.label: Devanagari Typography Chain (Geist → Noto Sans Devanagari)
nodes.rationale: Geist has zero Devanagari coverage and RN has no per-codepoint fallback to bundled fonts, so an AppText primitive detects the U+0900–U+097F range and applies Noto per run; OS fallback is unacceptable for a pixel-perfect commercial product.
nodes.norm_label: devanagari typography chain (geist → noto sans devanagari)

nodes.label: Formatting Law (formatInr, units never translated, Latin digits)
nodes.rationale: One money function everywhere — web, mobile, PDFs and voice-agent text — because raw Intl.NumberFormat would fragment Indian grouping across surfaces.
nodes.norm_label: formatting law (formatinr, units never translated, latin digits)

nodes.label: Per-Screen Definition of Done (12 items)
nodes.rationale: Applies unreduced to the 3D studio: full parity at 375px is the hardest and least negotiable commitment in the system.

nodes.label: N1–N10 Interaction & Accessibility Law
nodes.rationale: Promoted verbatim from the POC design brief when the 'Instrument' visual identity was retired; cited by number from several docs, so the numbering is fixed — never renumber, never reword an N-rule.

nodes.label: Mobile/Touch Contract (one canvas gesture vocabulary)
nodes.rationale: Build for pointer events and branch on capability, never on screen width; numeric entry is always available as the accessible and precise path beside every gesture.

nodes.label: Per-Tenant Branding — customer documents ONLY
nodes.rationale: Tenants brand what their customers see but never restyle the app, so every screenshot, support session and training video stays identical across tenants; palettes are never rejected — compliant shades are derived by computation and previewed live.

nodes.label: Adherence & Lint Intents (gated vs reviewed)
nodes.rationale: Raw hex is gated because it has a syntactic tell; arbitrary px and font-family are reviewed rather than gated because a grep there would be almost entirely false positives or 100% exemptions.

nodes.label: Block / Table / Zone is the editable unit above rooftop scale
nodes.rationale: The one structural decision that makes 100 MW possible — it is the industry paradigm, and scaling per-panel raycast with a BVH alone was rejected because it removes the O(n²) but still stores, edits and re-shades 150k objects: wrong abstraction, not a performance bug.
nodes.norm_label: block / table / zone is the editable unit above rooftop scale

nodes.label: Three Scale Regimes (rooftop / large C&I / utility)
nodes.rationale: Regime is a property of the design, not the tenant — a 100 kW rooftop and a 40 MW park coexist in one tenant, and the studio switches paradigm at the block boundary.
nodes.norm_label: three scale regimes (rooftop / large c&i / utility)

nodes.label: Scale Phase A (BVH, ProjectionContext, worker chunking, blocks schema)
nodes.rationale: Splits three ways — context injection and the blocks schema land at port time, BVH plus far-cap removal land immediately post-port as separate golden-verified changes, and GPU shading is Phase B, not A.
nodes.norm_label: scale phase a (bvh, projectioncontext, worker chunking, blocks schema)

nodes.label: Scale Phase B — Large C&I (block editing, GPU shading, server sims, LOD)
nodes.norm_label: scale phase b — large c&i (block editing, gpu shading, server sims, lod)

nodes.label: Scale Phase C — Utility (trackers, DEM terrain, block electrical, DXF)
nodes.norm_label: scale phase c — utility (trackers, dem terrain, block electrical, dxf)

nodes.label: GPU Shadow-Map Shading (288 sun-sample depth maps)
nodes.rationale: The published solar-cadaster technique: depth-map testing is far cheaper than ray intersection. GPU and CPU paths are pinned against each other by a ±2% tolerance test — one SHADING_ENGINE_VERSION, two executors.
nodes.norm_label: gpu shadow-map shading (288 sun-sample depth maps)

nodes.label: Single-Axis Tracker GCR Backtracking
nodes.rationale: Closed-form calculation mirroring pvlib's tracking.singleaxis, validated against pvlib reference vectors as a golden-file test; the 288-sample quadrature and depth-map path are unchanged — only instance matrices move.

nodes.label: GLO-30 DEM Terrain + terrain-aware row spacing
nodes.rationale: Closes the POC's deferred cliff exactly where its comment said 'real math and is deferred rather than approximated' — pitch per block computed from the block's fitted plane.
nodes.norm_label: glo-30 dem terrain + terrain-aware row spacing

nodes.label: Performance Budgets per Regime (release criteria)
nodes.rationale: A phase does not ship over budget; the block/table model keeps the utility column honest because 175k modules is ~4,000 tables, so the persisted and edited object count stays in the thousands at every regime.

nodes.label: Explicit Deferrals with Re-evaluation Triggers
nodes.rationale: Each deferral names the measurable condition that reopens it — terrain-following articulation, a server GPU farm, a Rust/WASM kernel, utility autorouting and WebXR are deferred with stated triggers rather than vague 'later'.

nodes.label: The Honesty Rule at Scale
nodes.rationale: Scale changes resolution, never honesty: provenance goes block-level with an aggregate inheriting the weakest tier of its members, the shading model's documented limits stay printed, and there is no express lane for money staleness during long recomputes.

nodes.label: Feature Matrix — HelioGrid v1 vs the field
nodes.norm_label: feature matrix — heliogrid v1 vs the field

nodes.label: Gap Verdicts (ADOPT-NOW / DESIGN-FOR / SKIP-DELIBERATELY)
nodes.rationale: Every gap gets a verdict so nothing is built by accident and nothing is left as an unexamined hole; DESIGN-FOR means the port or seam exists in v1 so the adapter lands later without rework.

nodes.label: ALMM/DCR Compliance Checking (ADOPT-NOW)
nodes.rationale: Elevated from data flags to a checked feature because it prevents the costliest rework in Indian EPC and only one competitor has it.

nodes.label: What Nobody Else Has (the moat)
nodes.rationale: Voice agent, provenance/honesty system, offline-first field app, vernacular UI, two-tier versioned catalog and org pricing with unlimited seats — competitors print confident numbers; HelioGrid prints defensible ones.

nodes.label: OpenSolar (free tier funded by placement + payments cut)
nodes.norm_label: opensolar (free tier funded by placement + payments cut)

nodes.label: UX Gap Register Rules (claim, close, never delete rows)
nodes.rationale: Each gap is designed at implementation time directly in the design system inside the module's build slice — there is no separate design phase, and the file is the single ledger so closed rows stay visible.
nodes.norm_label: ux gap register rules (claim, close, never delete rows)

nodes.label: UXG-11 — Named links + OTP-at-accept
nodes.rationale: A ₹92L C&I acceptance by 'whoever holds the URL' is the sharpest liability in the product, so the token scheme had to support named links from day one.

nodes.label: UXG-13 — Real billing suite (supersedes the D26-era mock)
nodes.norm_label: uxg-13 — real billing suite (supersedes the d26-era mock)

nodes.label: UXG-22 — Mode toolbar + touch gesture layer (2D canvas)
nodes.norm_label: uxg-22 — mode toolbar + touch gesture layer (2d canvas)

nodes.label: UXG-25 — Scale-program surfaces (blocks, trackers, DEM import)
nodes.norm_label: uxg-25 — scale-program surfaces (blocks, trackers, dem import)

nodes.label: UXG-A11Y-02 — --danger ↔ --surface measured ≈3.91:1 (CLOSED)
nodes.rationale: Ruling C's allowance was SC 1.4.11 non-text contrast, but a button's text label is governed by SC 1.4.3 and needs 4.5:1. Fixed at the token rather than the component, so the sub-AA annotation is retired rather than relaxed.

nodes.label: UXG-A11Y-03 — SegmentedControl inactive label ≈3.89:1 (CLOSED)
nodes.rationale: Found by hand, not by the coverage gate — proof of its documented blind spot: the track background and the label colour are set by different rules, so no single rule pairs the two. Fixing the token beat special-casing a component.

nodes.label: UXG-PAR-01 — RN cleared only part of the OTP error state (CLOSED)
nodes.rationale: The original finding was wrong and the correction matters more: RN did surface the failed resend, via a separate boolean rather than the shared union. The real divergence was narrower — web's single union cleared all three failures on edit while RN cleared one.
nodes.norm_label: uxg-par-01 — rn cleared only part of the otp error state (closed)

nodes.label: Scope Commitment (no Launch-2, no v1.1, no 'later' bucket)
nodes.rationale: The document was made DATELESS because reality invalidated the 20-day calendar and day numbers were being read as commitments they could no longer support; what governs is the track dependency structure, the launch gate and the risk register.
nodes.norm_label: scope commitment (no launch-2, no v1.1, no 'later' bucket)

nodes.label: Track F — Foundations + all external paperwork filed
nodes.norm_label: track f — foundations + all external paperwork filed

nodes.label: Track B — the money path & customer surface
nodes.norm_label: track b — the money path & customer surface

nodes.label: Track C — voice agent + awareness surfaces
nodes.norm_label: track c — voice agent + awareness surfaces

nodes.label: Track M — mobile in lockstep with web (not a phase)
nodes.rationale: A module with a mobile surface is not done until both its web and RN screens ship in the same slice from the same contract — mobile is never a follow-up task.
nodes.norm_label: track m — mobile in lockstep with web (not a phase)

nodes.label: Track D — THE STUDIO PORT (flagship, last by priority)
nodes.rationale: The census gate is a QUALITY gate and does not move for the calendar: if the track nears its end with census rows open, the release valve is dashboards and polish scope elsewhere, never census rows.
nodes.norm_label: track d — the studio port (flagship, last by priority)

nodes.label: Track E — offline layer + hardening + launch gate
nodes.rationale: Last track because nothing at launch depends on offline; until it lands, mobile is online-first behind repository interfaces so the swap is a data-layer change only.
nodes.norm_label: track e — offline layer + hardening + launch gate

nodes.label: LAUNCH GATE (all or no launch — 8 conditions)
nodes.norm_label: launch gate (all or no launch — 8 conditions)

nodes.label: Risk Register (with named release valves)
nodes.rationale: The only release valves are dashboard polish, funnel analytics depth and agent-performance screens — never money invariants, tenancy isolation, census rows, offline round-trip or provenance surfaces.

nodes.label: Third-Party Approval Clocks (DLT, Exotel KYC, Razorpay, store review)
nodes.rationale: All code ships regardless — these gates decide activation, not build; each is filed as early as possible with a documented fallback.
nodes.norm_label: third-party approval clocks (dlt, exotel kyc, razorpay, store review)

nodes.label: D1–D39 Conformance Table (HONORED / SUPERSEDED / PARTIAL)
nodes.rationale: A SUPERSEDED decision is dead — do not implement it, do not partially honour it; a PARTIAL row names exactly which half survives.

nodes.label: R2 — the full 9-stage project chain is canonical
nodes.norm_label: r2 — the full 9-stage project chain is canonical

nodes.label: R3 — Exotel + Sarvam behind our ports, Bolna as Plan B
nodes.norm_label: r3 — exotel + sarvam behind our ports, bolna as plan b

nodes.label: R4 — Razorpay in both roles (platform billing + BYO collections)
nodes.norm_label: r4 — razorpay in both roles (platform billing + byo collections)

nodes.label: R5 — PVGIS is the energy source of record; Google Solar is an enhancement
nodes.rationale: India coverage gaps make any Google dependency a product-breaking bet, so energy figures never silently switch source and the provenance line names the database.
nodes.norm_label: r5 — pvgis is the energy source of record; google solar is an enhancement

nodes.label: R6 (amended) — named links + OTP-at-accept ship at launch
nodes.norm_label: r6 (amended) — named links + otp-at-accept ship at launch

nodes.label: R9 — consolidated snooze / dormant / reopen state machine
nodes.rationale: Triggers and timers were scattered across three stages; this table is the single definition, all timers are BullMQ repeatables and all wake-ups land at 09:00 tenant-local so no screen invents a new timer.
nodes.norm_label: r9 — consolidated snooze / dormant / reopen state machine

nodes.label: R12 — free navigation; validation runs at Generate only
nodes.rationale: The Next-disabled rule is killed for the proposal builder, but the studio's electrical hard gate stays — it protects a physical system, not form completeness.
nodes.norm_label: r12 — free navigation; validation runs at generate only

nodes.label: R14 — the offline scope boundary (offline-full vs online-only)
nodes.norm_label: r14 — the offline scope boundary (offline-full vs online-only)

nodes.label: R18 — provenance tiers (measured / derived / estimated / assumed)
nodes.rationale: Adopted into packages/domain as a first-class type so the BOM's per-line confidence, the proposal's honesty labels and the customer link's disclaimers all read from one enum — no screen invents a fifth tier.
nodes.norm_label: r18 — provenance tiers (measured / derived / estimated / assumed)

nodes.label: Owner Directives §4 (absorbed from the archived BLUEPRINT)
nodes.rationale: Where a directive was later amended the amendment is stated FIRST and the superseded wording is marked as such — the archived file interleaved them, which let an agent quote stale law from above a correction.
nodes.norm_label: owner directives §4 (absorbed from the archived blueprint)

nodes.label: Subscription Lifecycle State Machine
nodes.rationale: Reactivation creates a NEW Razorpay subscription rather than resuming a halted one — a clean cut with one live mandate at a time; data is retained indefinitely regardless of how long the tenant was halted.

nodes.label: Soft-Block Matrix (per subscription state)
nodes.rationale: 'Paused' in late past_due covers only features that cost per-use money; core selling continues through the whole grace window, and the block is on new mutations from the UI, never on draining a field crew's already-captured queue.

nodes.label: Read + Export ALWAYS Work (product law)
nodes.rationale: Never hold an EPC's customer data hostage; no schema mechanism may do so, dunning copy carries no deletion threats because nothing is deleted, and customer links stay live in every billing state.

nodes.label: Razorpay Webhook Pipeline (verify → dedupe → fast 2xx → queue → poll)
nodes.rationale: Razorpay delivers at-least-once with duplicates and reordering guaranteed, so these patterns are mandatory rather than optional; reconciliation-by-poll should be boring, and any repair emits an alert.
nodes.norm_label: razorpay webhook pipeline (verify → dedupe → fast 2xx → queue → poll)

nodes.label: Entitlements Model — the ONLY runtime gating
nodes.rationale: There are no feature flags in this product; features ship enabled when merged, and the single runtime gate is plan entitlements plus usage allowances.
nodes.norm_label: entitlements model — the only runtime gating

nodes.label: Enforcement Points (the complete list)
nodes.rationale: Design capacity is gated at save/creation, never mid-edit, so the flagship is never interrupted per-keystroke; adding a gated feature means adding a row to this table.

nodes.label: Usage Metering (the ledger is the bill)
nodes.rationale: The tenant-visible usage screen shows exactly the rollups we enforce and bill from — same query, same numbers, no smoothing; if a bundle is 80% consumed the screen says so before the gate ever fires.
nodes.norm_label: usage metering (the ledger is the bill)

nodes.label: GST Invoicing (we are supplier of record)
nodes.rationale: Razorpay is a gateway, not merchant-of-record, so the GSTIN, remittance and IRN liability are ours; invoice rows already carry nullable IRN fields so crossing the e-invoicing threshold needs no backfill.
nodes.norm_label: gst invoicing (we are supplier of record)

nodes.label: Tenant Customer-Collections via BYO Razorpay
nodes.rationale: The platform never touching funds is the load-bearing regulatory line; Razorpay Route is rejected for now because it would make us the KYC-bearing master merchant with escrow obligations.

nodes.label: Refunds, Proration, Cancellation
nodes.rationale: Upgrades apply entitlements immediately because a paying customer should never wait; the downgrade screen shows exactly what will be blocked before confirming, and support credits are audited entitlement overrides rather than manual DB edits.

nodes.label: The Nine Laws (non-negotiable)
nodes.rationale: The repository — not any agent's memory — is the source of engineering truth, so the Laws live in one governance document that CLAUDE.md points to and the always-loaded rules file digests.

nodes.label: Law 4 — Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Duplicate definitions are defects, not conveniences: enums to contracts, visual values to generated tokens, schema to migrations, money formatting to formatInr, strings to the i18n catalog.

nodes.label: Law 7 — Cross-Platform Lockstep
nodes.rationale: Platform drift is a violation, not a follow-up; exceptions require an explicit owner ruling because the default is lockstep verified in the browser AND on both simulators.

nodes.label: Law 9 — Incremental Schema & API Growth
nodes.rationale: Big-bang schema implementation guarantees refactors and drift once real slices meet reality, so tables, enums, contracts and endpoints are authored only when their owning module's slice begins.

nodes.label: Decision Hierarchy (9 levels + two tiebreakers)
nodes.rationale: Never invent at level N what a higher level already defines; a per-package CLAUDE.md beats a cross-cutting rule because it is closer to the code, and a dated ADR beats a prose doc.

nodes.label: Rule → Mechanism Matrix (enforced / planned / prose)
nodes.rationale: A rule at stage 'prose' must say why no mechanism can hold it — that requirement is what stops prose quietly accumulating again. Notably, 'a fact both platforms need lives in a package' is enforced by nothing, because detecting it mechanically means comparing meaning, not text.

nodes.label: Traceability without a roadmap system (plans + .qa evidence)
nodes.rationale: Per-module roadmaps cost more to maintain than the traceability they bought and a stale roadmap actively misleads; status is never 'done' without evidence recording what was run, on what surface, and what was seen.
nodes.norm_label: traceability without a roadmap system (plans + .qa evidence)

nodes.label: Per-package CLAUDE.md template (landmines are mandatory)
nodes.rationale: Landmines do not count against the line budget: they are the healthiest part of the corpus and capping them would delete the incident record — an hour lost to a trap nobody wrote down is an hour the next person also loses.

nodes.label: Forward-Compatibility Register
nodes.rationale: Each row states what a module must build in NOW so a later module is not forced into a refactor; extracted from the build plan so it can be cited and read without loading the whole document.

nodes.label: The anti-collision device that makes Law 9 safe
nodes.rationale: A module may author only its own tables precisely because this register tells it which future needs its first migration must already satisfy; without it, module-by-module growth becomes short-sighted rather than incremental.
nodes.norm_label: the anti-collision device that makes law 9 safe

nodes.rationale: Everything here is product specification, not architecture or implementation guidance; the master spec is only safe to read through the spec-resolutions overlay because ~40% of the D-text is superseded.

nodes.rationale: The root requirement source for Law 6 traceability, but never cite a D-decision without checking its conformance row first — D3, D4, D12, D19, D26, D33 and D38 have all been overridden.

nodes.rationale: Most B2B SaaS asks for everything up front and people abandon, so onboarding asks only the minimum to produce one real quote and collects the rest when actually needed; a demo Pune rooftop exists because new users understand the product by opening something finished.

nodes.rationale: Duplicates are the one thing that kills solar CRMs: a homeowner who calls, fills a form and WhatsApps becomes three leads, three reps and three quotes for one very confused customer.

Offline is the normal case for physical capture, not the edge case.

nodes.label: ADR-0012: Voice agent — Exotel + Sarvam behind a thin orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Buy the two things we must never build in India (UL-VNO carrier licensing with DLT operations, Indic STT/TTS) and own the thin glue. Indian telecom law (TRAI/DLT, DND, 1600 vs 140x, CLI rules) plus DPDP residency rule out US-hosted voice stacks; the moat-bearing code is the orchestrator, so it stays ours and vendor-neutral.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0012: voice agent — exotel + sarvam behind a thin orchestrator

nodes.label: Exotel (TelephonyProvider)
nodes.rationale: UL-VNO-licensed carrier with the strongest DLT operations, AgentStream bidirectional WebSocket, IVR applets and DTMF.

nodes.label: Sarvam AI (SpeechProvider + LanguageModel)
nodes.rationale: Sovereign India compute keeps audio, transcripts and PII off US infrastructure; best-in-class Indic speech quality.

nodes.label: Saarika STT
nodes.rationale: Lowest WER in 13 of 15 Indian languages.

nodes.label: Bulbul TTS
nodes.rationale: Beats ElevenLabs on Hindi prosody.

nodes.label: CallSession orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Turn-taking, barge-in, AI disclosure within 30s, escalate-to-human and outcome classification are never vendor-specific — this is the glue we own.

nodes.label: ComplianceGate (non-swappable, ours)
nodes.rationale: Daily DND scrub, consent, 9am–9pm window and holiday calendar, 1600 vs 140x routing, keypress opt-out within 24h, 90-day recording retention. The ₹25,000-per-complaint penalty lands on the tenant as Principal Entity, so the gate must live in our code, not a vendor's.

nodes.label: Per-tenant voice usage metering
nodes.rationale: Every leg — telephony seconds, STT minutes, TTS chars, LLM tokens — is metered per tenant into the usage ledger; cost ≈ ₹2.5–4/min outbound all-in.

nodes.label: tenant_phone_numbers (per-tenant numbers, BYO)
nodes.rationale: Default platform Exophone; BYO via hosting/porting with KYC. TRAI CLI rules mean this is never caller-ID spoofing.

nodes.label: IVR in both directions
nodes.rationale: Inbound per-tenant flow builder (greeting → menu → AI / human / voicemail, business-hours aware); outbound DTMF traversal via sendDtmf/onDtmf with STT prompt detection.

nodes.label: Bolna (documented Plan B)
nodes.rationale: Strong India-native all-in-one (~₹6/min) but inheriting their agent runtime costs coarser cost/persona control — kept behind the same ports as Plan B rather than primary.

nodes.label: LiveKit self-host (v2 reference target)
nodes.rationale: Best long-term, but owning SIP trunking, DLT wiring and turn-taking tuning pre-launch is unaffordable; the port layer is designed toward it and it is deferred to v2.

nodes.label: DPDP residency constraint on voice data
nodes.rationale: Voice audio, transcripts and PII must not transit US infrastructure — this single constraint eliminates the entire US voice-agent vendor category.
nodes.norm_label: dpdp residency constraint on voice data

nodes.label: Rejected: Vapi / Retell / Bland
nodes.rationale: Audio transits US infra so DPDP residency fails; DLT support is bolt-on or absent and ₹-cost is no better.

nodes.label: Rejected: Sarvam Samvaad managed runtime
nodes.rationale: Sovereign and capable but launched early 2026 with unproven telephony/DLT maturity; buying the runtime dissolves the swap boundary.

nodes.label: Rejected: Pipecat
nodes.rationale: Python — breaks the TypeScript-everywhere rule.

nodes.label: Rejected: Twilio / Plivo / Knowlarity / Ozonetel
nodes.rationale: Cost, thin India DLT tooling, or weak streaming APIs respectively.

nodes.label: ADR-0013: Billing — Razorpay Subscriptions + in-house entitlements
nodes.rationale: Launch is next month and a second billing source of truth is unaffordable, so one INR rail with native trial support wins; platform SaaS billing and tenant customer collections must never be confused, and keeping funds out of our hands avoids RBI Payment Aggregator regulation.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0013: billing — razorpay subscriptions + in-house entitlements

nodes.label: UPI AutoPay mandate (primary rail)
nodes.rationale: ₹15,000/debit cap comfortably fits tier prices at ~0.5% + GST fees.

nodes.label: Trial-only, no free tier
nodes.rationale: 14-day full-feature trial with a single 7-day support extension, implemented by Razorpay's native trial support. A perpetual free tier breaks the capacity-tiered unit economics in docs/01.

nodes.label: At-least-once webhook handling
nodes.rationale: HMAC signature verify, dedupe on x-razorpay-event-id, fast-2xx plus queue, subscription.charged as the entitlement-granting event, API polling as reconciliation backstop.

nodes.label: In-house entitlements + usage on Postgres
nodes.rationale: plans, subscriptions, subscription_events, entitlements — a few days' work in NestJS versus a second source of truth; we own metering correctness.

nodes.label: usage_events append-only ledger
nodes.rationale: Voice minutes, AI detections, OTP and storage with period rollups; grant/expiry/rollup must be covered by the money-math invariants.

nodes.label: Soft-block enforcement; read + export always work
nodes.rationale: Product law: never hold tenant data hostage to billing state.
nodes.norm_label: soft-block enforcement; read + export always work

nodes.label: GST supplier-of-record obligations
nodes.rationale: Razorpay is a gateway, not merchant-of-record — GST-compliant invoices per cycle under our GSTIN/SAC, e-invoicing IRN validation ours, Razorpay's 18% GST on fees tracked separately.

nodes.label: PaymentLinkPort — BYO-Razorpay per tenant
nodes.rationale: Each EPC connects its own Razorpay account and funds settle directly to the EPC; onboarding friction is accepted as the price of staying unregulated.

nodes.label: Platform never touches funds (no RBI PA licence)
nodes.rationale: Aggregating collections would make us master merchant with KYC burden and drag us into Payment Aggregator territory.
nodes.norm_label: platform never touches funds (no rbi pa licence)

nodes.label: Rejected: Chargebee
nodes.rationale: ≈$7,188/yr, sits on top of Razorpay anyway, and adds a second source of truth for a single-currency launch.

nodes.label: Rejected: Zoho Billing
nodes.rationale: Cheap and GST-native but weak on usage-based pricing and declining mindshare.

nodes.label: Rejected: Stripe
nodes.rationale: Still not a general domestic India acquirer in 2026; only wins for USD billing abroad.

nodes.label: Rejected: platform-aggregated collections (Razorpay Route / Easy Split as default)
nodes.rationale: Kept strictly as an alternate adapter — as a default it makes us master merchant and drags us toward PA regulation.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: platform-aggregated collections (razorpay route / easy split as default)

nodes.label: ADR-0014: Scale program — block/table/zone, GPU shading, per-site origin
nodes.rationale: The design range is 1 kW → 100 MW (~150k+ modules) and the POC's single-origin projection, O(n²) CPU shading and per-panel editing all cliff at scale. Build the no-rewrite foundations now as investment INTO the studio, never as a reason to cut rooftop capability.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0014: scale program — block/table/zone, gpu shading, per-site origin

nodes.label: Block / table (rack) / zone data model
nodes.rationale: Above rooftop scale the editable unit is the block/table/zone with panels as derived instances; utility incumbents (HelioScope, PVcase, RatedPower) all abstract panels away because 150k independently editable panels is the wrong abstraction.

nodes.label: GPU shadow-map shading (three.js WebGPURenderer)
nodes.rationale: ~288 sun-sample depth maps sampled per module in a compute pass; WebGPU is baseline in 2026 with automatic WebGL2 fallback, so staying on WebGLRenderer leaves 2–10x on the table for no benefit.

nodes.label: three-mesh-bvh CPU/worker fallback and correctness oracle
nodes.rationale: Kept for precise near-field rooftop obstruction raycasts and as the oracle that keeps the GPU path honest; geometry is centred via BufferGeometry.center() to avoid float-precision loss at km scale.
nodes.norm_label: three-mesh-bvh cpu/worker fallback and correctness oracle

nodes.label: Per-site UTM/ENU origin via proj4js
nodes.rationale: Replaces the single equirectangular origin precisely because of float-precision loss at km scale.

nodes.label: Pure-TS kernels (Web Worker pool + Node worker_threads)
nodes.rationale: One codebase callable identically from browser and server jobs — no forked engine.
nodes.norm_label: pure-ts kernels (web worker pool + node worker_threads)

nodes.label: Single-axis trackers + closed-form GCR backtracking
nodes.rationale: A TS kernel mirroring pvlib.

nodes.label: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM terrain import
nodes.rationale: Free, global 30 m with SRTM fallback, meshed ground.

nodes.label: Float precision at km scale
nodes.rationale: The shared driver behind both geometry centring and the per-site origin change.

nodes.label: Two layout paradigms in one canonical Project model
nodes.rationale: Per-panel rooftop and block/table utility layouts must stay coherent; the one-frame gate and fingerprint recompute graph extend to cover both.
nodes.norm_label: two layout paradigms in one canonical project model

nodes.label: Deferred scale scope
nodes.rationale: Terrain-following tracker articulation, server GPU farm, utility-grade electrical autorouting and Rust/WASM kernels are explicitly deferred with reasons in docs/11.

nodes.label: Rejected: scaling per-panel CPU raycast (BVH only)
nodes.rationale: Removes O(n²) but still edits/stores/re-shades 150k objects; 150k selectable meshes stall rendering even instanced.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: scaling per-panel cpu raycast (bvh only)

nodes.label: Rejected: headless three.js on Node (headless-gl)
nodes.rationale: Fragile and unmaintained for GPU work; same-kernel-on-CPU now, Node WebGPU bindings later.

nodes.label: Rejected: Rust/WASM shading kernel
nodes.rationale: Violates the TS-domain rule and forks the engine; only ever justified as a profiled leaf.

nodes.label: Rejected: staying on WebGLRenderer
nodes.rationale: Forgoes compute-shader shading for no benefit given automatic fallback.

nodes.label: ADR-0015: i18n — Lingui v5, one catalog for Next.js and bare RN
nodes.rationale: One EN/HI/MR catalog must serve Next.js App Router (including RSC) and bare React Native, with per-user language switching that re-renders immediately (D25). Lingui is the only compile-time option that covers RN at all.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0015: i18n — lingui v5, one catalog for next.js and bare rn

nodes.label: Lingui v5
nodes.rationale: Compile-based (small bundles, native ICU MessageFormat) with a lightweight runtime for per-user locale switching; Next.js App Router + RSC officially supported.

nodes.label: @lingui/metro-transformer (bare RN)
nodes.rationale: Verified without Expo on RN ≥0.73 via babelTransformerPath plus po/pot sourceExts and FormatJS polyfills; flagged relatively new/beta and .po/.pot-only, so versions are pinned with a smoke check in the mobile CI lane.

nodes.label: Devanagari rendering (Noto Sans chain)
nodes.rationale: Explicit RN fallback handling is required.

nodes.label: D25 — per-user immediate locale switch
nodes.rationale: A Marathi surveyor and an English owner in the same company means the whole app re-renders on switch, without reloads — a runtime switch, not a build-time locale.

nodes.label: Natural-language message IDs require extraction discipline
nodes.rationale: Key type-safety comes from extraction plus messages.ts rather than typed functions, so copy edits change IDs.
nodes.norm_label: natural-language message ids require extraction discipline

nodes.label: Rejected: Paraglide (inlang)
nodes.rationale: Best-in-class type safety but no first-class React Native support — a dealbreaker for the field app.

nodes.label: Rejected: i18next
nodes.rationale: Runs everywhere but runtime-heavy, and key type-safety needs declaration-merging boilerplate agents get wrong.

nodes.label: Rejected: FormatJS / react-intl
nodes.rationale: Heavier and weaker RN DX.

nodes.label: ADR-0016: No feature-flag system — entitlements-only gating
nodes.rationale: Binding owner directive. Flag systems accrete permanent conditional debt, and for AI agents every flag doubles the code paths that must be reasoned about — dead branches are ambient falsehood that misleads an agent reading the code.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0016: no feature-flag system — entitlements-only gating

nodes.label: Entitlements are the only runtime gating
nodes.rationale: An entitlement row maps to a purchasable plan capability, never to a deploy stage — entitlements must not be abused as covert flags.
nodes.norm_label: entitlements are the only runtime gating

nodes.label: Trunk discipline — small complete verifiable slices
nodes.rationale: Features ship enabled when merged and incomplete work does not merge; large features must be decomposed into independently shippable slices — a forcing function accepted on purpose. Work that cannot be sliced waits on a branch, it does not merge dark.
nodes.norm_label: trunk discipline — small complete verifiable slices

nodes.label: No kill switch — rollback by redeploy
nodes.rationale: Fly Machines deploys make rollback minutes not hours, but it is honest to say incidents lose one mitigation lever; no gradual rollouts or canaries at the app layer, so risk management moves wholly to slice size and pre-merge verification.
nodes.norm_label: no kill switch — rollback by redeploy

nodes.label: ADR-0019: Telephony as a platform capability framework
nodes.rationale: Two forces broke the Exotel-shaped framing: the owner directive that telephony is a long-term PLATFORM capability which must never need refactoring to grow, and Spike S5 proving parts of the Exotel-shaped interface are not real on Exotel. nodes.rationale: placeOutbound, onInbound, mediaStream, hangup and getCapabilities are required of every adapter in packages/adapters/telephony — a small honest core instead of one grand interface.

nodes.rationale: Static, honest, per adapter+account flags (dtmfSend/Receive, transferCold/Warm, conference, recording, monitoring, voicemail, queueing, numberProvisioning, inboundIvr) — the Exotel adapter declares dtmfSend:false rather than hiding the gap in code paths.

nodes.label: Defined degradation ladder
nodes.rationale: A feature needing a missing capability degrades along the docs/07 §4 matrix — it never throws and never silently no-ops. Outbound IVR traversal needs dtmfSend; without it the campaign step is skipped and the call is flagged ivr_blocked for human follow-up.

nodes.label: CallOrchestrator (call-control plane)
nodes.rationale: Provider-agnostic owner of the call-leg state machine (ai_handling → handoff_pending → consulting → bridged → completed, plus callback_queued, voicemail, failed); executes routing plans, enforces ComplianceGate before every dial including consult legs, and writes the calls/call_handoffs ledger. Vendor adapters only move legs.

nodes.rationale: STT→LLM→TTS turn-taking, barge-in, AI disclosure ≤30s and outcome classification; talks only to SpeechProvider, LanguageModel and the media half of the core port.

Escalation chains are data, so the executor never changes to add a level.

nodes.rationale: Ordered levels with per-level ring timeout and no-answer fallthrough; the final fallback is ALWAYS callback queue or voicemail so a caller is never stranded.

nodes.rationale: Append-only summary, intent, sentiment, collected fields, transcript pointer, target, kind and outcome. The summary is generated ONCE at handoff decision time and pinned, so the human sees what the AI knew.
